content.content:
# AGENTS.md — PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

Handoff document for a coding agent (Codex, Claude Code, or any other) picking
up this project cold. Read this file first, then `LOG.md` for how the project
got here. `CLAUDE.md` covers the same ground for Claude sessions; where the two
disagree, this file's §3 file table is the current one.

Owner: Eric Rash. Last updated: 2026-09-14.

## Where this project lives

Working folder, Windows:
`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

This is Google Drive, not OneDrive. An earlier copy under
`OneDrive - Baylor University\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\...` no longer exists.
Older session logs and Codex rollouts still point at that OneDrive path; ignore
them and use the path above.

Workbooks, deliverables and the `Send/` folder stay here on Drive. Project
documentation and scripts are version controlled in the companion repo
`DEV\PP_Recruiting` (Windows: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\PP_Recruiting`,
Mac: `~/DEV/PP_Recruiting`), pushed to `erash11/PP_Recruiting`. Read that repo's
`docs/STATUS.md` before starting a session.

---

## 1. What this project is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
**Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles** with the internal **S.T.A.Q.S.**
grading scale, so incoming transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the
players who deserve a scout's time.

Two inputs, one system:

- The scout's **STAQS grade is the grade of record.**
- Telemetry percentiles are **threshold flags** that say who to review and which
  STAQS factors the data already supports.

Nothing is averaged, weighted, or blended into a composite. That was an explicit
design decision, not an oversight (§5).

Audience for the deliverables is recruiting and personnel staff, not analysts.

---

## 2. Standing rules (do not violate)

1. **Read-only in Telemetry.** Never edit, save, or submit anything in
   app.telemetry.fm. Scraping the rendered UI for read purposes is fine.
2. **Always create new files. Never overwrite.** Deliverables are numbered; the
   next revision is `006. ...`. The master `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` is
   never modified under any circumstances.
3. **Do not read Telemetry's auth token or import its internal service
   classes.** Both were tried and are blocked. Scrape the rendered table.
4. **STAQS is the grade of record.** Any data output is labeled a starting point
   for the scout, never a grade.
5. **Append to `LOG.md`** whenever a numbered file is created, a design decision
   is made or reversed, or a technique is proven or ruled out. Newest entries at
   the bottom, absolute dates.

---

## 3. Files in this folder

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` | **Master, read-only.** GRD SCALE, OFFENSE/DEFENSE EVAL KEY, SZ-SPD matrices, NIL/XFER pay scales, per-position tabs (QB, RB, WR, SLOT, TE, OT, OG, NT, END, JACK, ILB, CB, SAF, STAR, SPD). Authority for tiers and size-speed standards. Uses custom fonts (NCAA Baylor Bears, Bahnschrift). |
| `001. ... UNIFIED GRADING.xlsx` | Template workbook, 7 sample WRs, shows the format. 2026-09-02. |
| `001. ... FRAMEWORK.docx` | Written framework/explainer. |
| `002. ... UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026 LOADED).xlsx` | Proof of concept, 3,000 live portal players. 2026-09-03. |
| `003. ... COACH EXPLAINER.docx` | 6-page walkthrough of 002 for coaches/staff. |
| `003. ... UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx` | 002 restyled to the Baylor aesthetic. |
| `004. ... COACH BRIEF.docx` | 1.5-page version of the explainer. |
| `004. ... TEASER (AGM).docx` | One-page teaser for the assistant GM. |
| `005. ... TEASER (AGM, BAYLOR STYLE).docx` | 004 restyled off the 003 workbook. Current version of the teaser. |
| `CLAUDE.md` / `LOG.md` / `AGENTS.md` | Project context, development log, this handoff. |
| `_to_delete/` | Temp render artifacts. Session cannot delete files; move junk here. |

Build scripts (`build2.py`, `load.py`) lived in a session container and are
**not** in this folder. Their logic is documented on the workbook README tab, in
`LOG.md`, and in §5-6 below. **Rebuilding them as committed, versioned scripts
in this folder is the single highest-value thing a coding agent can do here.**

---

## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system

Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.

Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor).
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (001 / 002 / 003)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, band cut lines, simplified size standards by
  position. *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet, 67 columns in 002. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats. Percentiles 0-100; blank
  or `-` where a position carries no metric. Column order need not match
  Telemetry but **headers must**. HT in inches (6'1" = 73).
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row (3,154 in 002). Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite
  share, projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, critical
  deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values,
  best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
  the reliable definition source.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
  keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
  count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.

---

## 8. Current state

Proof of concept (002 / 003 xlsx) covers **3,000 portal players** who entered on
or after 1/1/2026 with 100+ snaps and an FBS/FCS previous team:

WR 453 · CB 431 · IDL 311 · EDGE 303 · SAF 290 · OB-LB 256 · RB 231 · OT 190 ·
QB 156 · TE 156 · OG 155 · C 68

Results as of 2026-09-03: **608 REVIEW flags** (144 of them uncommitted),
**32 AA** and **133 AL** projections.

Known data caution: Top End Speed (the raw mph field) has implausible scraped
values, e.g. 39 mph. Verify against Telemetry before quoting it. It feeds no
flag today.

Teaching case used in the coach-facing docs: **Michael Gravely Jr.** (SAF, Ball
State) — 5 elite of 7 traits, so an AL projection, but Player Impact in the 1st
percentile. The traits-versus-production example.

---

## 9. Next steps for an agent picking this up

Eric's stated next step: **once the approach is approved, automate the pull.**
Concretely, in priority order:

1. **Reconstruct the build as versioned code in this folder.** `build2.py`
   (workbook construction) and `load.py` (data load) exist only in a dead
   session container. Rebuild them from §5-6 with openpyxl so the workbook is
   reproducible from a data file rather than by hand.
2. **Automate the scrape** per §7, with the gotchas encoded as retries and
   assertions (the second Apply Filters click, the Filter (n) verification, the
   page-1 reload, export-before-reload).
3. **Add a refresh path** that regenerates the REVIEW BOARD against a new pull
   without touching prior numbered files. New pull = new numbered workbook.
4. **Add validation**: flag implausible raw values (Top End Speed), report trait
   coverage by position, and diff a new pull against the prior one so staff see
   who is newly flagged.

Things deliberately out of scope: a weighted composite score, any write
operation against Telemetry, and data-grading of FBI, wiring, keep-ability,
character, or medical.

## 1. What this project is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
**Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles** with the internal **S.T.A.Q.S.**
grading scale, so incoming transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the
players who deserve a scout's time.

Two inputs, one system:

- The scout's **STAQS grade is the grade of record.**
- Telemetry percentiles are **threshold flags** that say who to review and which
  STAQS factors the data already supports.

Nothing is averaged, weighted, or blended into a composite. That was an explicit
design decision, not an oversight (§5).

Audience for the deliverables is recruiting and personnel staff, not analysts.

## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system

Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.

Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor).
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

"""Load Telemetry leaderboard CSV exports into a new numbered grading workbook.

Reconstructs the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, for leaderboard exports
(Leaderboards > Player Traits / Advanced Stats > Download CSV) rather than the
Transfer Portal scrape.

Two stages:

1. Stage (always): read every CSV in --csv-dir, join Player Traits and Advanced
   Stats rows on PlayerId, map headers onto the template's PORTAL INPUT row 4,
   and write a staging CSV plus a report. No Excel needed.
2. Build (--out): copy the template to a NEW file and write PORTAL INPUT through
   Excel COM, so formulas, fonts and conditional formatting survive. openpyxl is
   used only to read; saving through it strips the conditional formatting.

The algorithm is not changed here. PORTAL INPUT columns A:BO keep their meaning,
so REVIEW BOARD formulas, traits graded and elite share are untouched. Extra
fields (PlayerId, raw position code, Elusiveness, source) go in columns after
Notes.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
      --csv-dir <folder of CSVs> --template <003 xlsx> --stage-dir <folder> ^
      [--min-elig 2] [--out <new 008 xlsx>]
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import shutil
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import openpyxl

HEADER_ROW = 4
FIRST_DATA_ROW = 5

# CSV header -> PORTAL INPUT header, where the names differ.
ALIASES = {
    "Pos.": "Pos (Telemetry)",
    "Team": "Prev Team",
    "Weight": "WT",
    "Elig.": "Elig Yrs",
    "Top End Speed": "Top End Speed (mph)",
    "Adj. Throw Velocity": "Adj Throw Vel",
    "Max Throw Velocity": "Max Throw Vel",
    "Deceleration": "Decel",
    "Completion Rate Over Expected": "Comp Rate Over Expected",
    "EPA/Target": "EPA Per Target",
}

# Handled explicitly, not copied straight across.
SPECIAL = {"Height", "Hometown", "State", "PlayerId", "Rank", "#"}

# Kept in extra columns after Notes.
EXTRA_COLUMNS = ["PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Elusiveness", "Source files"]

# Leaderboard position code -> POSITION MAP code (POSITION MAP tab, 003).
POSITION_CODES = {
    "QB": "QB",
    "RB": "RB", "HB": "RB", "FB": "RB",
    "WR": "WR", "OWR": "WR", "SWR": "WR", "ATH": "WR",
    "TE": "TE", "Y": "TE", "F": "TE", "H": "TE",  # Telemetry TE alignments
    "OT": "OT", "T": "OT", "LT": "OT", "RT": "OT",
    "OG": "OG", "G": "OG", "LG": "OG", "RG": "OG",
    "C": "C", "OC": "C",
    "IDL": "IDL", "DL": "IDL", "DT": "IDL", "NT": "IDL",
    "EDGE": "EDGE", "DE": "EDGE", "LE": "EDGE", "RE": "EDGE",
    "UP": "EDGE", "DOWN": "EDGE",  # Telemetry EDGE stance codes
    "OB-LB": "OB-LB", "LB": "OB-LB", "ILB": "OB-LB", "OLB": "OB-LB",  # OLB sits in OB-LB exports
    "MLB": "OB-LB", "WLB": "OB-LB", "SLB": "OB-LB",
    "CB": "CB", "LCB": "CB", "RCB": "CB", "NCB": "CB", "SCB": "CB", "OCB": "CB",
    "SAF": "SAF", "S": "SAF", "FS": "SAF", "SS": "SAF",
}

TEXT_COLUMNS = {"Player", "Pos (Telemetry)", "Class", "Prev Team", "Snaps detail",
                "Hometown", "High School", "Entered", "Committed To", "Risk Level",
                "Notes"}


def template_headers(template):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(template, read_only=True)
    row = next(wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=HEADER_ROW, max_row=HEADER_ROW,
                                           values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    return [h for h in row if h]


def height_inches(text):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"\s*(\d)-(\d{1,2}(?:\.\d)?)\s*", text or "")
    return int(m.group(1)) * 12 + float(m.group(2)) if m else None


def number(text):
    text = (text or "").strip()
    if text in ("", "-", "---"):
        return None
    try:
        value = float(text)
    except ValueError:
        return text
    return int(value) if value.is_integer() else value


def read_csvs(csv_dir, headers):
    known = set(headers)
    players = {}
    unmapped = Counter()
    raw_positions = Counter()
    for path in sorted(Path(csv_dir).glob("*.csv")):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
            for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                pid = row.get("PlayerId", "").strip()
                if not pid:
                    continue
                rec = players.setdefault(pid, {"PlayerId": pid, "Source files": set()})
                rec["Source files"].add(path.name)
                for col, val in row.items():
                    if col in SPECIAL:
                        continue
                    if col == "Elusiveness":
                        target = "Elusiveness"
                    else:
                        target = ALIASES.get(col, col)
                        if target not in known:
                            unmapped[col] += 1
                            continue
                    if rec.get(target) in (None, "") and val not in (None, ""):
                        rec[target] = val
                if row.get("Pos."):
                    raw_positions[row["Pos."]] += 1
                    rec.setdefault("Pos (raw)", row["Pos."])
                if rec.get("HT (in)") is None and row.get("Height"):
                    rec["HT (in)"] = height_inches(row["Height"])
                if not rec.get("Hometown") and row.get("Hometown"):
                    state = row.get("State", "").strip()
                    rec["Hometown"] = f"{row['Hometown']}, {state}" if state else row["Hometown"]
    return players, unmapped, raw_positions


def build_rows(players, headers, min_elig):
    rows, dropped = [], Counter()
    unknown_positions = Counter()
    for rec in players.values():
        raw = rec.get("Pos (raw)", "")
        code = POSITION_CODES.get(raw)
        if code is None:
            unknown_positions[raw] += 1
            code = raw
        rec["Pos (Telemetry)"] = code
        elig = number(rec.get("Elig Yrs"))
        if min_elig is not None and (not isinstance(elig, (int, float)) or elig < min_elig):
            dropped["below min elig"] += 1
            continue
        out = []
        for h in headers:
            val = rec.get(h)
            out.append(val if h in TEXT_COLUMNS or not isinstance(val, str) else number(val))
        out += [rec["PlayerId"], raw, number(rec.get("Elusiveness")),
                "; ".join(sorted(rec["Source files"]))]
        rows.append(out)
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (str(r[1]), str(r[0])))
    return rows, dropped, unknown_positions


def coverage(rows, headers):
    pos_i = headers.index("Pos (Telemetry)")
    trait_cols = headers[headers.index("Play Speed"):headers.index("Notes")]
    by_pos = defaultdict(lambda: Counter())
    counts = Counter()
    for r in rows:
        counts[r[pos_i]] += 1
        for c in trait_cols:
            if isinstance(r[headers.index(c)], (int, float)):
                by_pos[r[pos_i]][c] += 1
    return {p: {"players": counts[p], "non_blank": dict(by_pos[p])} for p in counts}


def write_stage(rows, headers, stage_dir, report):
    stage_dir = Path(stage_dir)
    stage_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(stage_dir / "portal_input_stage.csv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f)
        w.writerow(headers + EXTRA_COLUMNS)
        w.writerows(rows)
    (stage_dir / "load_report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")


def build_workbook(template, out, rows, headers):
    out = Path(out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite existing file: {out}")
    shutil.copy2(template, out)

    import win32com.client  # pywin32; Excel COM keeps formatting intact

    excel = win32com.client.DispatchEx("Excel.Application")
    excel.Visible = False
    excel.DisplayAlerts = False
    wb = excel.Workbooks.Open(str(out.resolve()))
    try:
        inp = wb.Worksheets("PORTAL INPUT")
        board = wb.Worksheets("REVIEW BOARD")
        width = len(headers) + len(EXTRA_COLUMNS)
        last_needed = FIRST_DATA_ROW + len(rows) - 1
        template_last = board.UsedRange.Row + board.UsedRange.Rows.Count - 1

        if last_needed > template_last:
            inp.Rows(template_last).Copy(inp.Range(f"A{template_last + 1}:A{last_needed}").EntireRow)
            board.Rows(template_last).Copy(board.Range(f"A{template_last + 1}:A{last_needed}").EntireRow)

        clear_to = max(last_needed, template_last)
        inp.Range(inp.Cells(FIRST_DATA_ROW, 1), inp.Cells(clear_to, width)).ClearContents()
        for i, name in enumerate(EXTRA_COLUMNS):
            inp.Cells(HEADER_ROW, len(headers) + 1 + i).Value = name

        chunk = 500
        for start in range(0, len(rows), chunk):
            block = rows[start:start + chunk]
            top = FIRST_DATA_ROW + start
            rng = inp.Range(inp.Cells(top, 1), inp.Cells(top + len(block) - 1, width))
            rng.Value = [tuple("" if v is None else v for v in r) for r in block]

        excel.CalculateFull()
        wb.Save()
    finally:
        wb.Close(SaveChanges=False)
        excel.Quit()


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--csv-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--template", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage-dir", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--min-elig", type=float, default=None,
                    help="keep players with Elig. at or above this. Telemetry's Elig. is the "
                         "current value in every season file, so 1 = still eligible after this "
                         "season (use 1 for a pre-portal pull)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", help="new workbook path; omit to stage only")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    headers = template_headers(args.template)
    players, unmapped, raw_positions = read_csvs(args.csv_dir, headers)
    rows, dropped, unknown_positions = build_rows(players, headers, args.min_elig)
    report = {
        "csv_files": sorted(p.name for p in Path(args.csv_dir).glob("*.csv")),
        "players_read": len(players),
        "rows_loaded": len(rows),
        "dropped": dict(dropped),
        "raw_position_codes": dict(raw_positions),
        "unknown_position_codes": dict(unknown_positions),
        "unmapped_csv_headers": dict(unmapped),
        "coverage_by_position": coverage(rows, headers),
    }
    write_stage(rows, headers, args.stage_dir, report)
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in report.items() if k != "coverage_by_position"}, indent=2))
    if args.out:
        build_workbook(args.template, args.out, rows, headers)
        print(f"Wrote {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 rows, 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** normalized name plus a compatible position group, then a check on
  the Telemetry team. All 19 matched one row. Jake Anderson has namesakes; the
  Illinois State NT (team code `ILST`, 624 snaps) is the one used. 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

| Baylor | Yakiri Walker | C | Memphis | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 91 |

| Baylor | Jamaal Whyce | IDL (DT) | Marshall | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 92 |

| Baylor | Kedrick Walker | OB-LB (ILB) | Georgia St | FRP | 3 / 7 | .43 | QS | +1 | Y | Y | 1 |
| Baylor | Stilton McKelvey | CB (OCB) | New Mexico St | FRP | 3 / 5 | .60 | QS | +1 | Y | | 76 |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the low trait in three of the four
   (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and Get Off is Whyce's
   other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Side notes

- Leaderboard `Team` is the 2025 school (slug for G6, code like `ILST` for FCS),
  not a current value, unlike `Elig.` and `Class`.
- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## 2026-09-16: Validation run, FCS and Group of Six half

formulas or SETTINGS changed, and no numbered file was created.

**Method:** the 19 players on 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only) with an FCS or
Group of Six previous team. `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` rebuilt the 22 fcs_g6
CSVs with no eligibility filter into a scratch workbook off Drive (14,068 rows),
because 10 of the 19 carry Elig 0 and are not in 008. Bands come from the
REVIEW BOARD formulas. Integrity check: all 8,761 008 players matched the
scratch build on band, share, REVIEW, speed alert and traits graded.

**Results:** bands exact for 6 of 19, within one tier for 16. REVIEW caught all
6 offensive players graded QS or better but only 1 of 6 on the defensive front
(Hjelle, Anderson, Whyce, Washington, Holloman missed: 1 elite IDL trait of 4,
Player Impact 82 to 96). It flagged 3 of 7 FRP-graded players; Hale (OG, AA
projection) and Kedrick Walker (ILB) both sit at Player Impact 1.

**Findings to decide on before 009:** a Player Impact or Advanced Stats alert
for the defensive front, a low Player Impact caution, whether Tackling belongs
in the IDL trait set, and whether the 2-trait OL set (bands can only be LIM/NGE,
QS or AA) needs another look. The sample has no LIM or NGE graded players, so
rejection is untested.

**Technique notes:** leaderboard `Team` is the season's school (not a current
value, unlike Elig and Class). Leaderboard `Top End Speed` looks like a
percentile, not mph.

Full table and questions: `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md` in the
`DEV/PP_Recruiting` repo.

**Next:** Eric reviews the findings; Power Four validation downloads (25 more
graded players); then 009.

# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 rows, 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** normalized name plus a compatible position group, then a check on
  the Telemetry team. All 19 matched one row. Jake Anderson has namesakes; the
  Illinois State NT (team code `ILST`, 624 snaps) is the one used. 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Other | Anthony Colandrea | QB | UNLV | AL | 5 / 10 | .50 | QS | -1 | Y | | 100 |
| Other | Kam Perry | WR (SWR) | Miami (OH) | AL | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | -1 | Y | | 93 |
| Other | Danny Scudero | WR (SWR) | San Jose St | QS | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | 0 | Y | Y | 90 |
| Other | Braden Pegan | WR (OWR) | Utah St | QS | 5 / 8 | .625 | AL | +1 | Y | Y | 98 |
| Other | Ben Murawski | OT (LT) | UConn | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 90 |
| Other | Joe Hjelle | IDL (DT) | Tulsa | AL | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -2 | | | 96 |
| Other | Jordan Sanders | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 2 / 4 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 82 |
| Other | Jake Anderson | IDL (NT) | Illinois St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 93 |
| Other | Harper Holloman | EDGE (UP) | W. Kentucky | AL | 1 / 6 | .17 | FRP | -2 | | | 93 |
| Baylor | Logan Moore | OT (RT) | UAB | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 78 |
| Baylor | Asher Hale | OG (RG) | S. Alabama | FRP | 2 / 2 | 1.00 | AA | +4 | Y | | 1 |
| Baylor | Yakiri Walker | C | Memphis | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 91 |
| Baylor | Cole Rhett | OT (RT) | Toledo | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 84 |
| Baylor | Jamaal Whyce | IDL (DT) | Marshall | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 92 |
| Baylor | Kam Washington | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 82 |
| Baylor | Jordan Mack | IDL (DT) | Coastal Carolina | FRP | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | 0 | | | 61 |
| Baylor | Garrick Ponder | EDGE (UP) | Southern Miss | FRP | 2 / 6 | .33 | FRP | 0 | | | 89 |
| Baylor | Kedrick Walker | OB-LB (ILB) | Georgia St | FRP | 3 / 7 | .43 | QS | +1 | Y | Y | 1 |
| Baylor | Stilton McKelvey | CB (OCB) | New Mexico St | FRP | 3 / 5 | .60 | QS | +1 | Y | | 76 |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the lowest trait for all four and a
   deficiency for three (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and
   Get Off is Whyce's other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Side notes

- Leaderboard `Team` is the 2025 school (slug for G6, code like `ILST` for FCS),
  not a current value, unlike `Elig.` and `Class`.
- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 1 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 1` keeps players still eligible after the current season. Telemetry's
  `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files (verified
  2026-09-15), so do not add a year for an older season.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

## Still missing

`build2.py`, the workbook construction script from 2026-09-03, is still lost.
`load_leaderboard.py` needs an existing workbook (003) as its template rather
than building one from scratch.

"""Compare REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP tab.

Validation run for the thresholds. Reads the graded players from 000 (read only),
finds each in a scratch workbook built by `load_leaderboard.py` with no
`--min-elig` (transferred players often carry Elig 0), and writes one row per
match with the band gap in tier steps. Bands come from the workbook's own
formulas, not a reimplementation.

Matching is normalized name plus a compatible position group. Telemetry team
names do not match the recap's abbreviations, so the team is printed for an
eyeball check instead of filtered on. Namesakes come out as AMBIGUOUS rows; keep
the one whose team matches.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
      --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
      --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
      --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
      [--baseline "<Drive>/008. ....xlsx"]

--baseline checks that every PlayerId in that workbook gets identical flags in
the scratch build. Any mismatch means the scratch build is wrong, not the
thresholds.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter

import openpyxl

TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
RECAP_TO_GROUPS = {
    "QB": {"QB"}, "RB": {"RB"}, "WR": {"WR"}, "TE": {"TE"},
    "OL": {"OT", "OG", "C"}, "IDL": {"IDL", "EDGE"}, "EDGE": {"EDGE", "IDL", "OB-LB"},
    "ILB": {"OB-LB"}, "LB": {"OB-LB"}, "CB": {"CB", "SAF"}, "SAF": {"SAF", "CB"},
}
FLAG_KEYS = ["Projected band", "Elite share", "REVIEW?", "Speed alert", "Traits graded"]
OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z ]", "", str(name).upper().replace(".", " ")).split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    inp = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    in_hdr, board_hdr = list(next(inp)), list(next(board))
    pid_i, raw_i, team_i = (in_hdr.index(h) for h in ("PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Prev Team"))
    out = {}
    for irow, brow in zip(inp, board):
        if irow[pid_i]:
            rec = dict(zip(board_hdr, brow))
            rec.update({"PlayerId": irow[pid_i], "Pos raw": irow[raw_i], "Team": irow[team_i]})
            out[irow[pid_i]] = rec
    wb.close()
    return out


def gap(band, rk):
    if band in TIERS and rk in TIERS:
        return TIERS.index(rk) - TIERS.index(band)
    return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prev-conf", required=True, help="comma list, e.g. G6,FCS or SEC,B12,B10,ACC")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    scratch = read_board(args.scratch)
    if args.baseline:
        base = read_board(args.baseline)
        missing = [p for p in base if p not in scratch]
        diff = [p for p in base if p in scratch and any(base[p][k] != scratch[p][k] for k in FLAG_KEYS)]
        print(f"integrity: {len(base)} baseline rows, {len(missing)} missing, {len(diff)} mismatched")

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}
    recap = [p for p in read_recap(args.master) if p["Prev conf"].upper() in confs]
    by_name = {}
    for rec in scratch.values():
        by_name.setdefault(tuple(norm(rec["Player"])), []).append(rec)

    out, status = [], Counter()
    for p in recap:
        groups = RECAP_TO_GROUPS.get(p["Recap pos"].upper(), set())
        hits = [r for r in by_name.get(tuple(norm(p["Recap name"])), []) if r["Pos"] in groups]
        match = "NONE" if not hits else "OK" if len(hits) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS"
        status[match] += 1
        for rec in hits or [{}]:
            row = {**p, "Match": match, **{k: rec.get(k) for k in OUT_FIELDS if k in rec}}
            row["Gap"] = gap(rec.get("Projected band"), p["Baylor RK"])
            out.append(row)

    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=OUT_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    print(f"{len(recap)} recap players, matches {dict(status)}; wrote {args.out}")
    for r in out:
        print(r["Match"], r["Recap pos"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Recap name"], "|", r.get("Pos"), r.get("Team"),
              r.get("Snaps"), "|", r.get("Projected band"), "gap", r["Gap"], "REVIEW", r.get("REVIEW?"),
              "PI", r.get("Player Impact"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}

"""Compare REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP tab.

Validation run for the thresholds. Reads the graded players from 000 (read only),
finds each in a scratch workbook built by `load_leaderboard.py` with no
`--min-elig` (transferred players often carry Elig 0), and writes one row per
match with the band gap in tier steps. Bands come from the workbook's own
formulas, not a reimplementation.

Matching is normalized name plus a compatible position group. Telemetry team
names do not match the recap's abbreviations, so the team is printed for an
eyeball check instead of filtered on. Namesakes come out as AMBIGUOUS rows; keep
the one whose team matches.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
      --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
      --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
      --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
      [--baseline "<Drive>/008. ....xlsx"]

--baseline checks that every PlayerId in that workbook gets identical flags in
the scratch build. Any mismatch means the scratch build is wrong, not the
thresholds.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter

import openpyxl

TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
RECAP_TO_GROUPS = {
    "QB": {"QB"}, "RB": {"RB"}, "WR": {"WR"}, "TE": {"TE"},
    "OL": {"OT", "OG", "C"}, "IDL": {"IDL", "EDGE"}, "EDGE": {"EDGE", "IDL", "OB-LB"},
    "ILB": {"OB-LB"}, "LB": {"OB-LB"}, "CB": {"CB", "SAF"}, "SAF": {"SAF", "CB"},
}
FLAG_KEYS = ["Projected band", "Elite share", "REVIEW?", "Speed alert", "Traits graded"]
OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    # 000 name cells can hold non-breaking spaces; treat any non-letter as a break.
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z']+", " ", str(name).upper()).replace("'", "").split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    inp = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    in_hdr, board_hdr = list(next(inp)), list(next(board))
    pid_i, raw_i, team_i = (in_hdr.index(h) for h in ("PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Prev Team"))
    out = {}
    for irow, brow in zip(inp, board):
        if irow[pid_i]:
            rec = dict(zip(board_hdr, brow))
            rec.update({"PlayerId": irow[pid_i], "Pos raw": irow[raw_i], "Team": irow[team_i]})
            out[irow[pid_i]] = rec
    wb.close()
    return out


def gap(band, rk):
    if band in TIERS and rk in TIERS:
        return TIERS.index(rk) - TIERS.index(band)
    return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prev-conf", required=True, help="comma list, e.g. G6,FCS or SEC,B12,B10,ACC")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    scratch = read_board(args.scratch)
    if args.baseline:
        base = read_board(args.baseline)
        missing = [p for p in base if p not in scratch]
        diff = [p for p in base if p in scratch and any(base[p][k] != scratch[p][k] for k in FLAG_KEYS)]
        print(f"integrity: {len(base)} baseline rows, {len(missing)} missing, {len(diff)} mismatched")

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}
    recap = [p for p in read_recap(args.master) if p["Prev conf"].upper() in confs]
    by_name = {}
    for rec in scratch.values():
        by_name.setdefault(tuple(norm(rec["Player"])), []).append(rec)

    out, status = [], Counter()
    for p in recap:
        groups = RECAP_TO_GROUPS.get(p["Recap pos"].upper(), set())
        name = norm(p["Recap name"])
        hits = [r for r in by_name.get(tuple(name), []) if r["Pos"] in groups]
        match = "NONE" if not hits else "OK" if len(hits) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS"
        if not hits and name:
            # Telemetry spells some first names differently (Kam / Kamren, Yakiri / Yakari).
            hits = [r for key, recs in by_name.items() if key and key[-1] == name[-1]
                    and key[0][0] == name[0][0] for r in recs if r["Pos"] in groups]
            match = "LOOSE" if hits else "NONE"
        status[match] += 1
        for rec in hits or [{}]:
            row = {**p, "Match": match, **{k: rec.get(k) for k in OUT_FIELDS if k in rec}}
            row["Gap"] = gap(rec.get("Projected band"), p["Baylor RK"])
            out.append(row)

    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=OUT_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    print(f"{len(recap)} recap players, matches {dict(status)}; wrote {args.out}")
    for r in out:
        print(r["Match"], r["Recap pos"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Recap name"], "|", r.get("Pos"), r.get("Team"),
              r.get("Snaps"), "|", r.get("Projected band"), "gap", r["Gap"], "REVIEW", r.get("REVIEW?"),
              "PI", r.get("Player Impact"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 players (two tables of 22), 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** normalized name plus a compatible position group, then a check on
  the Telemetry team. All 19 matched one row. Jake Anderson has namesakes; the
  Illinois State NT (team code `ILST`, 624 snaps) is the one used. 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

| Table | Player | Pos | 2025 team | Baylor RK | Traits (elite / graded) | Share | Band | Gap | REVIEW | Speed | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Other | Anthony Colandrea | QB | UNLV | AL | 5 / 10 | .50 | QS | -1 | Y | | 100 |
| Other | Kam Perry | WR (SWR) | Miami (OH) | AL | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | -1 | Y | | 93 |
| Other | Danny Scudero | WR (SWR) | San Jose St | QS | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | 0 | Y | Y | 90 |
| Other | Braden Pegan | WR (OWR) | Utah St | QS | 5 / 8 | .625 | AL | +1 | Y | Y | 98 |
| Other | Ben Murawski | OT (LT) | UConn | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 90 |
| Other | Joe Hjelle | IDL (DT) | Tulsa | AL | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -2 | | | 96 |
| Other | Jordan Sanders | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 2 / 4 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 82 |
| Other | Jake Anderson | IDL (NT) | Illinois St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 93 |
| Other | Harper Holloman | EDGE (UP) | W. Kentucky | AL | 1 / 6 | .17 | FRP | -2 | | | 93 |
| Baylor | Logan Moore | OT (RT) | UAB | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 78 |
| Baylor | Asher Hale | OG (RG) | S. Alabama | FRP | 2 / 2 | 1.00 | AA | +3 | Y | | 1 |
| Baylor | Yakiri Walker | C | Memphis | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 91 |
| Baylor | Cole Rhett | OT (RT) | Toledo | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 84 |
| Baylor | Jamaal Whyce | IDL (DT) | Marshall | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 92 |
| Baylor | Kam Washington | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 82 |
| Baylor | Jordan Mack | IDL (DT) | Coastal Carolina | FRP | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | 0 | | | 61 |
| Baylor | Garrick Ponder | EDGE (UP) | Southern Miss | FRP | 2 / 6 | .33 | FRP | 0 | | | 89 |
| Baylor | Kedrick Walker | OB-LB (ILB) | Georgia St | FRP | 3 / 7 | .43 | QS | +1 | Y | Y | 1 |
| Baylor | Stilton McKelvey | CB (OCB) | New Mexico St | FRP | 3 / 5 | .60 | QS | +1 | Y | | 76 |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the lowest trait for all four and a
   deficiency for three (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and
   Get Off is Whyce's other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Side notes

- Leaderboard `Team` is the 2025 school (slug for G6, code like `ILST` for FCS),
  not a current value, unlike `Elig.` and `Class`.
- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

# scripts

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 1 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 1` keeps players still eligible after the current season. Telemetry's
  `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files (verified
  2026-09-15), so do not add a year for an older season.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

I ran the validation step from the handoff: 008's projected bands against Baylor's own grades for the 19 FCS / Group of Six players on 000's `POST-PORTAL RECAP` tab. The flag rule works on offense but misses almost every good defensive lineman. No thresholds were changed.

**How I checked it:** I rebuilt the 2025 CSVs with no eligibility filter, because 10 of the 19 show Elig 0 and aren't in 008. The bands come from the workbook's own formulas. All 8,761 players in 008 get identical flags in that rebuild. The committed script reproduces all 19 rows.

**Results:**
- **Band agreement:** 6 of 19 exact, 16 within one tier. Three are off by two or more: Hjelle (AL graded, FRP projected), Holloman (AL, FRP) and Hale (FRP, AA). The projection runs low at the top: none of the 4 AL-graded players projects AL.
- **Offense:** REVIEW caught all 6 players Baylor graded QS or better.
- **Defensive front:** REVIEW caught 1 of 6. Hjelle, Anderson, Whyce, Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) have 1 elite trait of 4 (6 for Holloman), mostly pulled down by Tackling or Get Off. Their Player Impact is 82 to 96, so the Advanced Stats saw them, but those stats don't feed REVIEW.
- **FRP-graded players flagged:** 3 of 7. Hale (2 of 2 offensive line traits, so an automatic AA) and Kedrick Walker both have Player Impact in the 1st percentile, the same pattern as the Gravely teaching case.
- **Offensive line bands:** with only 2 traits, a lineman can only land LIM/NGE, QS or AA.
- **Limits:** only 19 players, and nobody Baylor graded LIM or NGE, so how well REVIEW screens out weak players is untested.

**Decisions for you** (listed at the end of the validation doc):
1. Should a defensive lineman with high Player Impact get a separate alert, the way the speed alert works? It would stay a threshold flag, not a composite.
2. Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows?
3. Should Tackling count as an IDL trait?
4. Should the Power Four downloads (25 more graded players) come before 009?

**Also found:**
- Telemetry spells three first names differently from 000 (Jacob Anderson, Yakari Walker, Kamren Washington). They matched on last name plus first initial, confirmed by team and position.
- The leaderboard `Team` column is the 2025 school, unlike Elig and Class.
- Leaderboard `Top End Speed` looks like a percentile, not mph.

**Where it lives:** branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915`, pushed and in sync with the remote, still not merged to main.
- `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`: full table, observations and questions.
- `scripts/validate_recap.py`: the matching script, kept for the Power Four rerun, with usage in `scripts/README.md`.
- `docs/STATUS.md`: updated.
- A dated entry added to `LOG.md` on Drive.

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 007 is the latest, so the next
  one is 008.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

# Memory Index — DEV

- [Sports teams](user_sports-teams.md) — follows the Indiana Fever (WNBA); default team for ambiguous WNBA asks
- [Zero-edit YouTube pipeline](reference_zero-edit-youtube-pipeline.md) — Jack Roberts' 5-phase Claude Code video system; full note in vault Knowledge/frameworks/
- [Working-conditions bottleneck](user_working-conditions-bottleneck.md) — limiter is conditions not effort; company generates his ideas and solitude refines them, plus a permission gate on acting unasked — be the thinking partner in-session
- [DEV layout and discovery](project_dev-layout-and-discovery.md) — one folder per project, depth-2 scan limit, and never store source under a gitignored subtree
- [KeystoneOS verification habits](project_keystoneos-verification-habits.md) — which state claims mislead (run-ledger, memsearch streaks, worktree tests) and why to re-check before asserting
- [Git Bash MSYS/AD stall](project_git-bash-msys-ad-stall.md) — why bash randomly dies with `add_item errno 1`: AD lookup exceeds MSYS2's 15s spinlock; fix via nsswitch files-only + `shell: powershell` hooks
- [Backup task sleep-kill signature](project_backup-task-sleepkill-signature.md) — DailyBackup exit 3221225786 + same-day clean log = benign sleep interruption, not rot
- [Tech inventory refresh](project_tech-inventory-refresh.md) — 09-16 run: 52 resp, 32/32 units (VB answered), merged to main; synced workbook renumbers IDs, match on timestamps

    for v in r["rows"]:
        if v["Pos"] in COUNTED and v["Team"] in ("tulsa", "ILST", "western-ky", "marshall", "texas-st", "coastal-caro", "southern-miss"):
            t = v["traits"]; c = [k for k in COUNTED[v["Pos"]] if isinstance(t.get(k), (int, float))]
            el = sum(t[k] >= 75 for k in c); c2 = [k for k in c if k != "Tackling"]; el2 = sum(t[k] >= 75 for k in c2)
            print(r["name"], v["Pos"], "with tackling", el, "/", len(c), "without", el2, "/", len(c2), round(el2 / len(c2), 3))

    new = Counter(); newfront = Counter()
    for x in ok:
