# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 players (two tables of 22), 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** `scripts/validate_recap.py`, normalized name plus a compatible
  position group, then a check on the Telemetry team. 16 matched exactly. Three
  are spelled differently in Telemetry and matched on last name plus first
  initial, confirmed by team and position: Jacob Anderson (Illinois State NT,
  `ILST`, 624 snaps), Yakari Walker (Memphis C) and Kamren Washington (Texas
  State DT). 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

| Table | Player | Pos | 2025 team | Baylor RK | Traits (elite / graded) | Share | Band | Gap | REVIEW | Speed | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Other | Anthony Colandrea | QB | UNLV | AL | 5 / 10 | .50 | QS | -1 | Y | | 100 |
| Other | Kam Perry | WR (SWR) | Miami (OH) | AL | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | -1 | Y | | 93 |
| Other | Danny Scudero | WR (SWR) | San Jose St | QS | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | 0 | Y | Y | 90 |
| Other | Braden Pegan | WR (OWR) | Utah St | QS | 5 / 8 | .625 | AL | +1 | Y | Y | 98 |
| Other | Ben Murawski | OT (LT) | UConn | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 90 |
| Other | Joe Hjelle | IDL (DT) | Tulsa | AL | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -2 | | | 96 |
| Other | Jordan Sanders | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 2 / 4 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 82 |
| Other | Jake Anderson | IDL (NT) | Illinois St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 93 |
| Other | Harper Holloman | EDGE (UP) | W. Kentucky | AL | 1 / 6 | .17 | FRP | -2 | | | 93 |
| Baylor | Logan Moore | OT (RT) | UAB | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 78 |
| Baylor | Asher Hale | OG (RG) | S. Alabama | FRP | 2 / 2 | 1.00 | AA | +3 | Y | | 1 |
| Baylor | Yakiri Walker | C | Memphis | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 91 |
| Baylor | Cole Rhett | OT (RT) | Toledo | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 84 |
| Baylor | Jamaal Whyce | IDL (DT) | Marshall | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 92 |
| Baylor | Kam Washington | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 82 |
| Baylor | Jordan Mack | IDL (DT) | Coastal Carolina | FRP | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | 0 | | | 61 |
| Baylor | Garrick Ponder | EDGE (UP) | Southern Miss | FRP | 2 / 6 | .33 | FRP | 0 | | | 89 |
| Baylor | Kedrick Walker | OB-LB (ILB) | Georgia St | FRP | 3 / 7 | .43 | QS | +1 | Y | Y | 1 |
| Baylor | Stilton McKelvey | CB (OCB) | New Mexico St | FRP | 3 / 5 | .60 | QS | +1 | Y | | 76 |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the lowest trait for all four and a
   deficiency for three (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and
   Get Off is Whyce's other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Side notes

- Leaderboard `Team` is the 2025 school (slug for G6, code like `ILST` for FCS),
  not a current value, unlike `Elig.` and `Class`.
- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 008 are on Drive. **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS +
  Group of Six leaderboard baseline: 8,761 players with Elig 1+, 879 REVIEW
  flags, 778 of them with Sample OK. Built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from
  22 CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. Next number is 009.
- 2026-09-15 meeting with a player personnel staff member: strong buy-in; he
  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run
  (FCS / G6 half done 2026-09-16), screening matrix (009), then the weekly
  refresh once 2026 data fills in.
- **Validation run, FCS / G6 half (2026-09-16):** 19 graded players from 000
  `POST-PORTAL RECAP`. Bands: 6 exact, 16 within one tier. REVIEW caught 6 of 6
  offensive QS-or-better players but only 1 of 6 on the defensive front (IDL
  1 of 4 elite traits, Player Impact 82 to 96). It flagged 3 of 7 FRP players,
  two with Player Impact 1. No thresholds changed. Detail:
  `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.
- This work is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (pushed), not
  yet merged to main. Detail: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. **Eric reviews the validation findings** and answers the questions at the
   end of `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md` (front-line Player Impact alert,
   low Player Impact caution, IDL Tackling, P4 downloads before 009).
2. **Validation downloads** for the 25 Power Four players on that tab: 2025,
   scope FBS + FCS, 9 position groups x Player Traits + Advanced Stats = 18 CSVs
   into `_exports/2025_baseline/validation_fbs_fcs/` (folder exists, empty).
   Eric approved these downloads. Rerun the same method: `load_leaderboard.py`
   with no `--min-elig` into a scratch folder off Drive (10 of the 19 FCS / G6
   players carry Elig 0 and are not in 008).
3. **Deliverable 009, the screening matrix**, drafted from the validation
   results. See `docs/open-work.md`.
4. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in (weeks 5 to 6). The staff member
   runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the workbook.
5. Reconstruct `build2.py` (workbook construction). `load_leaderboard.py`
   covers the data load for leaderboard exports.

## Open questions

- Are the 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds useful for recruiting?
  First test (FCS / G6, n = 19): good on offense, misses the defensive front,
  and the 2-trait OL set can only produce LIM/NGE, QS or AA. The sample has no
  LIM or NGE graded players, so rejection is untested.
- Elusiveness (Telemetry WR trait) is missing from the CROSSWALK, glossary and
  formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability descriptor says "Elusive."
  Add it as a counted trait (changes WR elite share) or as a secondary?
- SETTINGS has no SLOT size row, so slot receivers are sized against WR.
- Size versus Player Impact for proven undersized players; band sort versus a
  rank, given the no-composite rule.
- Merge `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` into main?
- Drive `CLAUDE.md` file table is stale, and Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 wrongly says
  only PORTAL INPUT headers must match.

## Gotchas

- REVIEW BOARD reads PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position, not header. Load
  with `load_leaderboard.py`; write workbooks only through Excel COM (openpyxl
  save strips the conditional formatting).
- Telemetry `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files
  (30 of 30 transfers matched). Elig 1+ means still eligible after this season.
  `Team` is the season's school, not a current value. Leaderboard `Top End
  Speed` looks like a percentile, not mph.
- Leaderboard position codes are alignments: OWR/SWR, H/F/Y, LT/RT, LG/C/RG,
  DT/NT, UP/DOWN, ILB/OLB, FS/SS, OCB/SCB, ST. Both scripts map them; ST shows
  Baylor tab "?".
- 4,047 of 8,761 rows in 008 are NO DATA: Advanced-Stats-only players carry
  Player Impact but no traits. FCS has no Ball Skills values. 66 players sit in
  two position groups and keep the first file's position.
- Telemetry in the browser: Chrome's "Ask where to save each file" dialog
  freezes automation (Eric turned it off 2026-09-15). Switching Player Traits /
  Advanced Stats tabs resets season, scope and group. Scope "Clear selection"
  does not remove Power Four; untick the option. Click coordinates use the
  screenshot frame, not page pixels. The Advanced Stats group list adds K and P

  came back empty).
- Portal scrape: calendar arrows move two months; "Apply Filters" may need a
  second click; reload if Next is disabled on page 1; the table is virtualized

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
entries.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
entries.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool
entries.description: Execute JavaScript code in the context of the current page. The code runs in the page's context and can interact with the DOM, window object, and page variables. Returns the result of the last expression or any thrown errors. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. You can access and modify the DOM, call page functions, and interact with page variables.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the code in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
entries.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
entries.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp

Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 008 are on Drive. **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS +
  Group of Six leaderboard baseline: 8,761 players with Elig 1+, 879 REVIEW
  flags, 778 of them with Sample OK. Built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from
  22 CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. Next number is 009.
- 2026-09-15 meeting with a player personnel staff member: strong buy-in; he
  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run
  (FCS / G6 half done 2026-09-16), screening matrix (009), then the weekly
  refresh once 2026 data fills in.
- **Validation run, FCS / G6 half (2026-09-16):** 19 graded players from 000
  `POST-PORTAL RECAP`. Bands: 6 exact, 16 within one tier. REVIEW caught 6 of 6
  offensive QS-or-better players but only 1 of 6 on the defensive front (IDL
  1 of 4 elite traits, Player Impact 82 to 96). It flagged 3 of 7 FRP players,
  two with Player Impact 1. No thresholds changed. Detail:
  `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.
- This work is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (pushed), not
  yet merged to main. Detail: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. **Decided 2026-09-16** (see "Decisions" in the validation doc): add a
   Player Impact alert that fires like the speed alert; add a low Player Impact
   alert (a note, not a suppression); Tackling stays counted for IDL (removing
   it fixes none of the misses); do the Power Four run before 009. Cut points
   for both alerts are picked after the Power Four run, using the sizing table
   in the validation doc.
2. **Validation downloads** for the 25 Power Four players on that tab: 2025,
   scope FBS + FCS, 9 position groups x Player Traits + Advanced Stats = 18 CSVs
   into `_exports/2025_baseline/validation_fbs_fcs/` (folder exists, empty).
   Eric approved these downloads. Rerun the same method: `load_leaderboard.py`
   with no `--min-elig` into a scratch folder off Drive (10 of the 19 FCS / G6
   players carry Elig 0 and are not in 008).
3. **Deliverable 009, the screening matrix**, drafted from the validation
   results. See `docs/open-work.md`.
4. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in (weeks 5 to 6). The staff member
   runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the workbook.
5. Reconstruct `build2.py` (workbook construction). `load_leaderboard.py`
   covers the data load for leaderboard exports.

## Open questions

- Are the 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds useful for recruiting?
  First test (FCS / G6, n = 19): good on offense, misses the defensive front,
  and the 2-trait OL set can only produce LIM/NGE, QS or AA. The sample has no
  LIM or NGE graded players, so rejection is untested.
- Elusiveness (Telemetry WR trait) is missing from the CROSSWALK, glossary and
  formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability descriptor says "Elusive."
  Add it as a counted trait (changes WR elite share) or as a secondary?
- SETTINGS has no SLOT size row, so slot receivers are sized against WR.
- Size versus Player Impact for proven undersized players; band sort versus a
  rank, given the no-composite rule.
- Merge `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` into main?
- Drive `CLAUDE.md` file table is stale, and Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 wrongly says
  only PORTAL INPUT headers must match.

## Gotchas

- REVIEW BOARD reads PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position, not header. Load
  with `load_leaderboard.py`; write workbooks only through Excel COM (openpyxl
  save strips the conditional formatting).
- Telemetry `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files

  `Team` is the season's school, not a current value. Leaderboard `Top End
  Speed` looks like a percentile, not mph.
- Leaderboard position codes are alignments: OWR/SWR, H/F/Y, LT/RT, LG/C/RG,

- 4,047 of 8,761 rows in 008 are NO DATA: Advanced-Stats-only players carry

"""Local-only CSV receiver: the Telemetry page POSTs CSV text, saved into OUT."""
import re
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer
from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path(r"C:/Users/eric_rash/.claude/jobs/94392fa1/tmp/p4_capture")
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def _cors(self):
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "https://app.telemetry.fm")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "POST, OPTIONS")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network", "true")

    def do_OPTIONS(self):
        self.send_response(204); self._cors(); self.end_headers()

    def do_POST(self):
        name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]", "_", self.path.strip("/")) or "unnamed.csv"
        body = self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0)))
        (OUT / name).write_bytes(body)
        self.send_response(200); self._cors(); self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(f"saved {name} {len(body)}".encode())


HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8765), H).serve_forever()

"""Compare REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP tab.

Validation run for the thresholds. Reads the graded players from 000 (read only),
finds each in a scratch workbook built by `load_leaderboard.py` with no
`--min-elig` (transferred players often carry Elig 0), and writes one row per
match with the band gap in tier steps. Bands come from the workbook's own
formulas, not a reimplementation.

Matching is normalized name plus a compatible position group. Telemetry team
names do not match the recap's abbreviations, so the team is printed for an
eyeball check instead of filtered on. Namesakes come out as AMBIGUOUS rows; keep
the one whose team matches. With no exact name, it falls back to last name plus
first initial and marks every candidate LOOSE; confirm those by team too.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
      --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
      --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
      --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
      [--baseline "<Drive>/008. ....xlsx"]

--baseline checks that every PlayerId in that workbook gets identical flags in
the scratch build. Any mismatch means the scratch build is wrong, not the
thresholds.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter

import openpyxl

TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
RECAP_TO_GROUPS = {
    "QB": {"QB"}, "RB": {"RB"}, "WR": {"WR"}, "TE": {"TE"},
    "OL": {"OT", "OG", "C"}, "IDL": {"IDL", "EDGE"}, "EDGE": {"EDGE", "IDL", "OB-LB"},
    "ILB": {"OB-LB"}, "LB": {"OB-LB"}, "CB": {"CB", "SAF"}, "SAF": {"SAF", "CB"},
}
FLAG_KEYS = ["Projected band", "Elite share", "REVIEW?", "Speed alert", "Traits graded"]
OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    # 000 name cells can hold non-breaking spaces; treat any non-letter as a break.
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z']+", " ", str(name).upper()).replace("'", "").split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    inp = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    in_hdr, board_hdr = list(next(inp)), list(next(board))
    pid_i, raw_i, team_i = (in_hdr.index(h) for h in ("PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Prev Team"))
    out = {}
    for irow, brow in zip(inp, board):
        if irow[pid_i]:
            rec = dict(zip(board_hdr, brow))
            rec.update({"PlayerId": irow[pid_i], "Pos raw": irow[raw_i], "Team": irow[team_i]})
            out[irow[pid_i]] = rec
    wb.close()
    return out


def gap(band, rk):
    if band in TIERS and rk in TIERS:
        return TIERS.index(rk) - TIERS.index(band)
    return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prev-conf", required=True, help="comma list, e.g. G6,FCS or SEC,B12,B10,ACC")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    scratch = read_board(args.scratch)
    if args.baseline:
        base = read_board(args.baseline)
        missing = [p for p in base if p not in scratch]
        diff = [p for p in base if p in scratch and any(base[p][k] != scratch[p][k] for k in FLAG_KEYS)]
        print(f"integrity: {len(base)} baseline rows, {len(missing)} missing, {len(diff)} mismatched")

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}
    recap = [p for p in read_recap(args.master) if p["Prev conf"].upper() in confs]
    by_name = {}
    for rec in scratch.values():
        by_name.setdefault(tuple(norm(rec["Player"])), []).append(rec)

    out, status = [], Counter()
    for p in recap:
        groups = RECAP_TO_GROUPS.get(p["Recap pos"].upper(), set())
        name = norm(p["Recap name"])
        hits = [r for r in by_name.get(tuple(name), []) if r["Pos"] in groups]
        match = "NONE" if not hits else "OK" if len(hits) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS"
        if not hits and name:
            # Telemetry spells some first names differently (Kam / Kamren, Yakiri / Yakari).
            hits = [r for key, recs in by_name.items() if key and key[-1] == name[-1]
                    and key[0][0] == name[0][0] for r in recs if r["Pos"] in groups]
            match = "LOOSE" if hits else "NONE"
        status[match] += 1
        for rec in hits or [{}]:
            row = {**p, "Match": match, **{k: rec.get(k) for k in OUT_FIELDS if k in rec}}
            row["Gap"] = gap(rec.get("Projected band"), p["Baylor RK"])
            out.append(row)

    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=OUT_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    print(f"{len(recap)} recap players, matches {dict(status)}; wrote {args.out}")
    for r in out:
        print(r["Match"], r["Recap pos"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Recap name"], "|", r.get("Pos"), r.get("Team"),
              r.get("Snaps"), "|", r.get("Projected band"), "gap", r["Gap"], "REVIEW", r.get("REVIEW?"),
              "PI", r.get("Player Impact"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    # 000 name cells can hold non-breaking spaces; treat any non-letter as a break.
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z']+", " ", str(name).upper()).replace("'", "").split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    inp = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    in_hdr, board_hdr = list(next(inp)), list(next(board))
    pid_i, raw_i, team_i = (in_hdr.index(h) for h in ("PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Prev Team"))
    out = {}
    for irow, brow in zip(inp, board):
        if irow[pid_i]:
            rec = dict(zip(board_hdr, brow))
            rec.update({"PlayerId": irow[pid_i], "Pos raw": irow[raw_i], "Team": irow[team_i]})
            out[irow[pid_i]] = rec
    wb.close()
    return out


def gap(band, rk):
    if band in TIERS and rk in TIERS:
        return TIERS.index(rk) - TIERS.index(band)
    return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prev-conf", required=True, help="comma list, e.g. G6,FCS or SEC,B12,B10,ACC")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    scratch = read_board(args.scratch)
    if args.baseline:
        base = read_board(args.baseline)
        missing = [p for p in base if p not in scratch]
        diff = [p for p in base if p in scratch and any(base[p][k] != scratch[p][k] for k in FLAG_KEYS)]
        print(f"integrity: {len(base)} baseline rows, {len(missing)} missing, {len(diff)} mismatched")

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}
    recap = [p for p in read_recap(args.master) if p["Prev conf"].upper() in confs]
    by_name = {}
    for rec in scratch.values():
        by_name.setdefault(tuple(norm(rec["Player"])), []).append(rec)

    out, status = [], Counter()
    for p in recap:
        groups = RECAP_TO_GROUPS.get(p["Recap pos"].upper(), set())
        name = norm(p["Recap name"])
        hits = [r for r in by_name.get(tuple(name), []) if r["Pos"] in groups]
        match = "NONE" if not hits else "OK" if len(hits) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS"
        if not hits and name:
            # Telemetry spells some first names differently (Kam / Kamren, Yakiri / Yakari).
            # Last names within a typo (Osunsamni / Osunsanmi) also count.
            hits = [r for key, recs in by_name.items() if key and key[0][0] == name[0][0]
                    and SequenceMatcher(None, key[-1], name[-1]).ratio() >= 0.85
                    for r in recs if r["Pos"] in groups]
            match = "LOOSE" if hits else "NONE"
        status[match] += 1
        for rec in hits or [{}]:
            row = {**p, "Match": match, **{k: rec.get(k) for k in OUT_FIELDS if k in rec}}
            row["Gap"] = gap(rec.get("Projected band"), p["Baylor RK"])
            out.append(row)

    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=OUT_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    print(f"{len(recap)} recap players, matches {dict(status)}; wrote {args.out}")
    for r in out:
        print(r["Match"], r["Recap pos"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Recap name"], "|", r.get("Pos"), r.get("Team"),
              r.get("Snaps"), "|", r.get("Projected band"), "gap", r["Gap"], "REVIEW", r.get("REVIEW?"),
              "PI", r.get("Player Impact"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import csv
T = r"C:/Users/eric_rash/.claude/jobs/94392fa1/tmp/"
TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
OFF = {"QB", "WR", "OL", "RB", "TE"}
rows = []
for half, f in (("FCS/G6", "validation_regress.csv"), ("P4", "validation_p4.csv")):
    for r in csv.DictReader(open(T + f, encoding="utf-8")):
        if r["Recap name"] == "JAKE ANDERSON" and r["Team"] != "ILST":
            continue
        r["half"] = half
        rows.append(r)

def num(x):
    try: return float(x)
    except: return None

for half in ("FCS/G6", "P4", "ALL"):
    rs = [r for r in rows if (half == "ALL" or r["half"] == half) and r["Projected band"] in TIERS and r["Sample"] == "OK"]
    gaps = [int(r["Gap"]) for r in rs]
    print(f"\n== {half}: banded n={len(rs)}  exact={gaps.count(0)} within1={sum(abs(g)<=1 for g in gaps)} off2+={sum(abs(g)>=2 for g in gaps)}"
          f"  neg={sum(g<0 for g in gaps)} zero={gaps.count(0)} pos={sum(g>0 for g in gaps)} mean={sum(gaps)/len(gaps):.2f}")
    good = [r for r in rs if r["Baylor RK"] in ("AA", "AL", "QS")]
    frp = [r for r in rs if r["Baylor RK"] == "FRP"]
    for side, test in (("offense", lambda r: r["Recap pos"] in OFF), ("defense", lambda r: r["Recap pos"] not in OFF)):
        g = [r for r in good if test(r)]
        print(f"  QS+ {side}: REVIEW {sum(r['REVIEW?']=='Y' for r in g)}/{len(g)}")
    print(f"  FRP flagged: {sum(r['REVIEW?']=='Y' for r in frp)}/{len(frp)}")
    misses = [r for r in good if r["REVIEW?"] != "Y"]
    fr_non = [r for r in frp if r["REVIEW?"] != "Y"]
    for thr in (80, 85, 90):
        c = [r["Recap name"] for r in misses if (num(r["Player Impact"]) or 0) >= thr]
        fp = [r["Recap name"] for r in fr_non if (num(r["Player Impact"]) or 0) >= thr]
        print(f"  PI>={thr}: catches {len(c)}/{len(misses)} misses {c}; also alerts FRP {len(fp)}/{len(fr_non)} {fp}")
    low = [(r["Recap name"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Player Impact"]) for r in rs if r["REVIEW?"] == "Y" and (num(r["Player Impact"]) or 99) <= 10]
    print(f"  REVIEW with PI<=10: {low}")
    print("  never caught:", [r["Recap name"] for r in misses if (num(r["Player Impact"]) or 0) < 80])

# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 players (two tables of 22), 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** `scripts/validate_recap.py`, normalized name plus a compatible
  position group, then a check on the Telemetry team. 16 matched exactly. Three
  are spelled differently in Telemetry and matched on last name plus first
  initial, confirmed by team and position: Jacob Anderson (Illinois State NT,
  `ILST`, 624 snaps), Yakari Walker (Memphis C) and Kamren Washington (Texas
  State DT). 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

| Table | Player | Pos | 2025 team | Baylor RK | Traits (elite / graded) | Share | Band | Gap | REVIEW | Speed | Player Impact |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the lowest trait for all four and a
   deficiency for three (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and
   Get Off is Whyce's other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Decisions (Eric, 2026-09-16)

1. **Player Impact alert: yes.** It works like the speed alert: its own flag,
   firing independently of the elite-share gate. Not a composite.
2. **Low Player Impact: note it, as its own alert** (not a suppression of
   REVIEW).
3. **Tackling: stays a counted IDL trait.** Eric deferred; the data decides it.
   Removing Tackling fixes none of the five misses: each goes from 1 of 4 elite
   to 1 of 3 (.333), still under .375. The misses come from the small IDL
   trait set, and alert 1 is what catches them. Eric may still raise Tackling
   with the personnel staff.
4. **Power Four validation downloads before 009**, so the matrix does not rest
   on 19 players.

|---|---|---|
| Player Impact 85+, not already REVIEW | 649 | 4 (Hjelle, Anderson, Holloman, Whyce) |
| Player Impact 90+, not already REVIEW | 385 | 4 (Washington, 82, still missed) |
| Player Impact 95+, not already REVIEW | 187 | 1 (Hjelle) |
| REVIEW with Player Impact 5 or lower | 94 | Hale, Kedrick Walker (both 1) |
| REVIEW with Player Impact 10 or lower | 138 | Hale, Kedrick Walker |

At 90+, the new alert is spread across positions (CB 78, WR 61, SAF 60, EDGE
41, OB-LB 36, IDL 35), so it is not only a front-line fix. Whether to limit it
to IDL and EDGE is open until the P4 run. Cut points are set after that run,
not now.

- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 008 are on Drive. **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS +
  Group of Six leaderboard baseline: 8,761 players with Elig 1+, 879 REVIEW
  flags, 778 of them with Sample OK. Built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from
  22 CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. Next number is 009.
- 2026-09-15 meeting with a player personnel staff member: strong buy-in; he
  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run
  (FCS / G6 half done 2026-09-16), screening matrix (009), then the weekly
  refresh once 2026 data fills in.
- **Validation run, FCS / G6 half (2026-09-16):** 19 graded players from 000
  `POST-PORTAL RECAP`. Bands: 6 exact, 16 within one tier. REVIEW caught 6 of 6
  offensive QS-or-better players but only 1 of 6 on the defensive front (IDL
  1 of 4 elite traits, Player Impact 82 to 96). It flagged 3 of 7 FRP players,
  two with Player Impact 1. No thresholds changed. Detail:
  `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.
- This work is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (pushed), not
  yet merged to main. Detail: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. **Decided 2026-09-16** (see "Decisions" in the validation doc): add a
   Player Impact alert that fires like the speed alert; add a low Player Impact
   alert (a note, not a suppression); Tackling stays counted for IDL (removing
   it fixes none of the misses); do the Power Four run before 009. Cut points
   for both alerts are picked after the Power Four run, using the sizing table
   in the validation doc.
2. **Validation downloads** for the 25 Power Four players on that tab: 2025,
   scope FBS + FCS, 9 position groups x Player Traits + Advanced Stats = 18 CSVs
   into `_exports/2025_baseline/validation_fbs_fcs/` (folder exists, empty).
   Eric approved these downloads. **In progress 2026-09-16: 1 of 18 filed**
   (`2025_fbs-fcs_QB_player-traits.csv`, 716 rows). The page froze after the
   first download and a second never landed, likely a Chrome prompt (multiple
   downloads) that automation cannot see. Percentiles do not change with scope
   (Colandrea's QB values match the fcs_g6 file). Rerun the same method: `load_leaderboard.py`
   with no `--min-elig` into a scratch folder off Drive (10 of the 19 FCS / G6
   players carry Elig 0 and are not in 008).
3. **Deliverable 009, the screening matrix**, drafted from the validation
   results. See `docs/open-work.md`.
4. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in (weeks 5 to 6). The staff member
   runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the workbook.
5. Reconstruct `build2.py` (workbook construction). `load_leaderboard.py`
   covers the data load for leaderboard exports.

## Open questions

- Are the 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds useful for recruiting?
  First test (FCS / G6, n = 19): good on offense, misses the defensive front,
  and the 2-trait OL set can only produce LIM/NGE, QS or AA. The sample has no
  LIM or NGE graded players, so rejection is untested.
- Elusiveness (Telemetry WR trait) is missing from the CROSSWALK, glossary and
  formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability descriptor says "Elusive."
  Add it as a counted trait (changes WR elite share) or as a secondary?
- SETTINGS has no SLOT size row, so slot receivers are sized against WR.
- Size versus Player Impact for proven undersized players; band sort versus a
  rank, given the no-composite rule.
- Merge `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` into main?
- Drive `CLAUDE.md` file table is stale, and Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 wrongly says
  only PORTAL INPUT headers must match.

## Gotchas

- REVIEW BOARD reads PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position, not header. Load
  with `load_leaderboard.py`; write workbooks only through Excel COM (openpyxl
  save strips the conditional formatting).
- Telemetry `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files
  (30 of 30 transfers matched). Elig 1+ means still eligible after this season.
  `Team` is the season's school, not a current value. Leaderboard `Top End
  Speed` looks like a percentile, not mph.
- Leaderboard position codes are alignments: OWR/SWR, H/F/Y, LT/RT, LG/C/RG,
  DT/NT, UP/DOWN, ILB/OLB, FS/SS, OCB/SCB, ST. Both scripts map them; ST shows
  Baylor tab "?".
- 4,047 of 8,761 rows in 008 are NO DATA: Advanced-Stats-only players carry
  Player Impact but no traits. FCS has no Ball Skills values. 66 players sit in
  two position groups and keep the first file's position.
- Telemetry in the browser: Chrome's "Ask where to save each file" dialog
  freezes automation (Eric turned it off 2026-09-15). Switching Player Traits /
  Advanced Stats tabs resets season, scope and group. Scope "Clear selection"
  does not remove Power Four; untick the option. Click coordinates use the
  screenshot frame, not page pixels. The Advanced Stats group list adds K and P
  at the bottom. Check the table has rows before Download CSV (one TE export
  came back empty).
- Portal scrape: calendar arrows move two months; "Apply Filters" may need a
  second click; reload if Next is disabled on page 1; the table is virtualized
  (~20 rows in the DOM).

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 008 are on Drive. **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS +
  Group of Six leaderboard baseline: 8,761 players with Elig 1+, 879 REVIEW
  flags, 778 of them with Sample OK. Built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from
  22 CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. Next number is 009.

  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run (done
  2026-09-16), screening matrix (009), then the weekly refresh once 2026 data
  fills in.

  `POST-PORTAL RECAP` with a band (19 FCS / G6, 20 Power Four). Bands: 12
  exact, 28 within one tier, and the data runs low (mean gap -0.77 tiers,
  -1.25 on Power Four). REVIEW caught 10 of 13 QS-or-better offensive players
  and 5 of 15 defensive players; it flagged 4 of 11 FRP players. No thresholds
  changed. Detail: `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.

  yet merged to main. Detail: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. **Decided 2026-09-16** (see "Decisions" in the validation doc): add a
   Player Impact alert that fires like the speed alert; add a low Player Impact
   alert (a note, not a suppression); Tackling stays counted for IDL (removing
   it fixes none of the misses); do the Power Four run before 009. Cut points
   for both alerts are picked after the Power Four run, using the sizing table
   in the validation doc.

   scope FBS + FCS, 9 position groups x Player Traits + Advanced Stats = 18 CSVs
   into `_exports/2025_baseline/validation_fbs_fcs/` (folder exists, empty).

   first download and a second never landed, likely a Chrome prompt (multiple
   downloads) that automation cannot see. Percentiles do not change with scope
   (Colandrea's QB values match the fcs_g6 file). Rerun the same method: `load_leaderboard.py`
   with no `--min-elig` into a scratch folder off Drive (10 of the 19 FCS / G6
   players carry Elig 0 and are not in 008).
3. **Deliverable 009, the screening matrix**, drafted from the validation
   results. See `docs/open-work.md`.

   runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the workbook.

   covers the data load for leaderboard exports.

  Four grades (8 of 9 AL-graded P4 players project below AL). The 2-trait OL set
  can only produce LIM/NGE, QS or AA. No LIM or NGE graded players in the
  sample, so rejection is untested.

  Coleman QS to FRP with Player Impact 96, Lagway AL to NGE)?

  confirm same player.

  formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability descriptor says "Elusive."
  Add it as a counted trait (changes WR elite share) or as a secondary?

- Size versus Player Impact for proven undersized players; band sort versus a
  rank, given the no-composite rule.

# scripts

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 1 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 1` keeps players still eligible after the current season. Telemetry's
  `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files (verified
  2026-09-15), so do not add a year for an older season.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

## validate_recap.py

Validation run: compares REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's
`POST-PORTAL RECAP` tab (read only). First used 2026-09-16; results in
`docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.

```
uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
    --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
    --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
    --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
    [--baseline "<Drive>/008. <name>.xlsx"]
```

- Build `--scratch` with `load_leaderboard.py` and **no** `--min-elig`, into a
  scratch folder off Drive. Transferred players often carry Elig 0.
- `--prev-conf` picks recap rows by previous conference (`SEC,B12,B10,ACC` for
  the Power Four half).
- Match column: OK, AMBIGUOUS (namesakes), LOOSE (last name plus first initial,
  for spellings like Kam / Kamren), NONE. Confirm AMBIGUOUS and LOOSE rows by
  team before using them.
- `--baseline` checks the scratch build gives identical flags for every PlayerId
  in a numbered workbook.

## Still missing

`build2.py`, the workbook construction script from 2026-09-03, is still lost.
`load_leaderboard.py` needs an existing workbook (003) as its template rather
than building one from scratch.

content.text:
The Power Four half of the validation is done, so the check now covers 39 graded players. It's committed and pushed. The main finding: the data projects lower than Baylor's grades, especially for Power Four players. The one open call is where to set the Player Impact alert.

**How the data got pulled:** after you allowed multiple downloads, Chrome still wouldn't save a second scripted download while its window was hidden. So I read the CSV Telemetry builds for the Download CSV button straight from the page and kept only the recap players' rows.
- **Files:** 18 are in `_exports/2025_baseline/validation_fbs_fcs/`. The two QB files are full exports. The other 16 end in `_recap-subset.csv` and hold only recap players.
- **Why subsets are enough:** a player's percentiles don't change with scope, so each recap player grades exactly as a full file would.
- **Their limit:** they can't be used to estimate how many players an alert adds.
- **Checks:** every subset file matched the page's character count. After loosening the name matcher, the first 19 players still match the same way.

**Power Four results (20 players with a band):**
- **Band agreement:** 6 exact, 12 within one tier. 13 project lower than Baylor's grade and only 1 higher; the average is -1.25 tiers.
- **Top grades:** of 9 AL-graded players, only DeAndre Moore projects AL.
- **Biggest disagreements are Baylor's own players:** Keaton Thomas (AL graded, LIM projected, 0 of 7 elite traits), DJ Coleman (QS, FRP, Player Impact 96) and DJ Lagway (AL, NGE).
- **Not a defensive-line problem only:** the new misses are Finau and Chester (OL), Romaine, Rich, Coleman and Ryan Davis (defense), and Lagway (QB).
- **Speed alert:** it caught Tobi Osunsanmi (Play Speed 99), which is what it's for.

**Combined (39 players):**
- **Band agreement:** 12 exact, 28 within one tier.
- **REVIEW on players Baylor graded QS or better:** offense 10 of 13, defense 5 of 15.
- **REVIEW on FRP players:** 4 of 11.

**Your decision: the Player Impact alert cut point.** REVIEW missed 13 players graded QS or better:

| Cut point | Misses caught | FRP players it would also alert | Added names on 008 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 90+ | 6 of 13 | 1 of 7 | 385 |
| 80+ | 9 of 13 | 4 of 7 | not sized |

85+ catches the same 6 as 90+ but alerts more FRP players, so the real choice is 90 or 80. My lean is 90: it's cleaner, and 80 alerts most of the FRP players REVIEW correctly skipped. Keaton Thomas, Rich, Lagway and Ryan Davis aren't caught at any cut point.

**Low Player Impact alert (10 or under, on REVIEW rows):** it fires on Hale and Kedrick Walker (both FRP) and Gilmore (QS). It works as a note, and Gilmore is why it shouldn't suppress anything.

**Loose ends:**
- **Debraun Hampton** has no 2025 row at WR, RB or TE.
- **Jordan Church** matched a Louisville guard in Telemetry, while the recap says N. Carolina St. Same name and position, but worth confirming.

Everything is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915`, still not merged to main:
- `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`: full tables.
- `docs/STATUS.md`: updated, including the browser workaround as a gotcha.
- `scripts/validate_recap.py`: the name matcher now tolerates small spelling differences.
- `LOG.md` on Drive: a dated entry.

# Open work: the position-by-position screening matrix

This is deliverable 009. It was renumbered on 2026-09-15: Eric approved running
the 2025 baseline load (008) first, so the matrix is drafted from what that
validation run shows. It was started on 2026-09-05 and never finished. Source criteria were gathered, approval was asked for, and the
session ended before anything was written.

## What it needs to be

A one-page decision matrix defining, per position, the minimum evidence that
earns a further look, which weaknesses are acceptable, and what the exception
paths are. Concrete proposed rules, not blanks for staff to fill in.

Label everything in it as proposed staff-review decisions, not as existing
workbook rules. The workbook's current thresholds are implemented but unproven.

## What Eric specified

- "Let's proceed with the first priority in the position-by-position matrix."
- "Propose minimums and exceptions for review."
- "There is also a role-mapping issue within the first gap: WR versus SLOT, END
  versus JACK, and CB versus STAR can have different requirements."
- "The thresholds haven't demonstrated recruiting usefulness yet."
- "Test known prospects, including players the filter misses. Measure both
  worthwhile reviews generated and worthwhile players overlooked, by position."
- "minimum thresholds for guys that are worth taking a further look at"

Do not collapse those roles into generic position groups.

## Role factors already in the workbook

| Role | Factors used |
|---|---|
| END | Strength at POA, Tackling, Block Destruction / Pass Rush |
| JACK | Pass Rush / Block Destruction, Tackling, Ability to Play in Space |
| CB | Man-to-Man Coverage, Transition Speed / Competitive Edge, Ball Skills |
| STAR | Man-to-Man Coverage, Tackling, Ball Skills |
| WR and SLOT | Shared core evaluation factors, separate size matrices |

## Telemetry to Baylor role mapping

- WR maps to WR, SLOT
- EDGE maps to END, JACK
- CB maps to CB, STAR
- SAF maps to SAF, STAR
- OB-LB maps to ILB, JACK
- C is graded on the OG/C tab

## Metric quirks to keep in mind

Traits and advanced stats are 0 to 100 percentiles against the same position
(FBS, 2019 to present). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph, QB Risk Level is a
text label, Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the portal grid, QB
decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection", DB coverage surfaces as
"EPA/Target".

Source: Codex session 01a0718d, 2026-09-05. The quoted lines above are Eric's
own words from that session. Everything else is drawn from the workbook and the
Drive folder's AGENTS.md.

A1 'TELEMETRY X S.T.A.Q.S. UNIFIED GRADING'
A2 'BAYLOR PLAYER PERSONNEL // S.T.A.Q.S. GRADING SYSTEM // TELEMETRY CROSSWALK'
A3 'Couples Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal STAQS grade tiers so new portal data can be filtered for review.'
A4 'WHAT THIS IS'
B4 "One system, two inputs. The scout's STAQS grade (8 factors x 1/3/9, total 8-72) stays the grade of record. Telemetry percentiles are turned into threshold flags"
A5 'THE BRIDGE'
B5 'Your GRD SCALE already defines each tier by elite-trait count (AA 7-8, AL 5-6, QS 3-4, FRP 1-2, LIM 0-1, NGE 0). A Telemetry percentile at or above the Elite th'
A6 'HOW TO USE'
B6 '1) In Telemetry, filter Transfer Portal to a position, open Player Traits then Advanced Stats, and Export.  2) Paste values into PORTAL INPUT (yellow cells only'
A7 'SCOPE'
B7 'Telemetry percentiles compare a player to FBS players at his position (2019-present, in-game tracking). This applies to portal and current-roster evaluation. Hi'
A8 'WHAT THE DATA CAN AND CANNOT GRADE'

"""Add the Player Impact alert and Low Impact alert to a grading workbook.

Decided by Eric 2026-09-16 after the validation run
(docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md):

- Impact alert: Player Impact at or above SETTINGS (90). Fires on its own, like
  the speed alert, and turns REVIEW? on for rows with trait data. It also fires
  on NO DATA rows (Advanced Stats only) so staff can filter for them, but REVIEW
  keeps its existing rule that a row with no graded traits is never REVIEW.
- Low Impact alert: a REVIEW row with Player Impact at or below SETTINGS (10).
  A note only; it never suppresses REVIEW.

Copies --in to a NEW --out file and edits the copy through Excel COM (openpyxl
save strips conditional formatting). Inserting through COM shifts every
existing reference. The source workbook is never modified.

Layout after the change:
  SETTINGS rows 11-12 = the two new cut points (band table moves down 2 rows)
  REVIEW BOARD N = Impact alert, O = Low Impact alert (after Size-Speed alert)

Usage:
  uv run --with pywin32 python scripts/add_impact_alerts.py --in <008 xlsx> --out <009 xlsx>
"""

import argparse
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

XL_PASTE_FORMATS = -4122

SETTINGS_ROWS = [
    ("Player Impact alert: Player Impact at or above", 90,
     "Fires on its own, like the speed alert, and turns REVIEW on. Validation 2026-09-16: "
     "catches 6 of 13 QS-or-better players the trait gate missed. Also shown on NO DATA rows."),
    ("Low Impact alert: REVIEW rows with Player Impact at or below", 10,
     "A caution note only, never suppresses REVIEW. Traits look good, production does not "
     "(Hale, Kedrick Walker; Gilmore was graded QS)."),
]

IMPACT = ("=IF('PORTAL INPUT'!A5=\"\",\"\",IF(AND('PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5<>\"\","
          "N('PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5)>=SETTINGS!$B$11),\"Y\",\"\"))")
LOW_IMPACT = ("=IF('PORTAL INPUT'!A5=\"\",\"\",IF(AND(K5=\"Y\",'PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5<>\"\","
              "N('PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5)<=SETTINGS!$B$12),\"Y\",\"\"))")
REVIEW = ("=IF('PORTAL INPUT'!A5=\"\",\"\",IF(F5=0,\"\",IF(OR(AND(F5>=SETTINGS!$B$10,"
          "I5>=SETTINGS!$B$9),L5=\"Y\",N5=\"Y\"),\"Y\",\"\")))")

README_NOTE = (" Impact alert (SETTINGS): Player Impact at or above the cut point flags a row"
               " on its own, like the speed alert, and turns REVIEW on when the row has trait"
               " data. Low Impact alert: a REVIEW row with very low Player Impact, a caution"
               " note only.")


def cf_count(wb):
    return {ws.Name: ws.Cells.FormatConditions.Count for ws in wb.Worksheets}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--in", dest="src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    src, out = Path(args.src), Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite existing file: {out}")
    shutil.copy2(src, out)

    import win32com.client

    excel = win32com.client.DispatchEx("Excel.Application")
    excel.Visible = False
    excel.DisplayAlerts = False
    wb = excel.Workbooks.Open(str(out.resolve()))
    try:
        before = cf_count(wb)
        settings = wb.Worksheets("SETTINGS")
        board = wb.Worksheets("REVIEW BOARD")
        if str(board.Range("L4").Value) != "Speed alert" or str(board.Range("M4").Value) != "Size-Speed alert":
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD layout is not the expected 003/008 layout; stopping.")
        if "Player Impact alert" in str(settings.Range("A11").Value or ""):
            raise SystemExit("Workbook already has the Impact alert settings; stopping.")

        # SETTINGS: two new rows after the existing settings (rows 5-10).
        settings.Rows("11:12").Insert()
        settings.Range("A10:C10").Copy()
        settings.Range("A11:C12").PasteSpecial(XL_PASTE_FORMATS)
        for i, (label, value, note) in enumerate(SETTINGS_ROWS):
            row = 11 + i
            settings.Cells(row, 1).Value = label
            settings.Cells(row, 2).Value = value
            settings.Cells(row, 3).Value = note

        # REVIEW BOARD: two columns after Size-Speed alert, formatted like Speed alert.
        last = board.UsedRange.Row + board.UsedRange.Rows.Count - 1
        board.Columns("N:O").Insert()
        board.Columns("L").Copy()
        board.Columns("N:O").PasteSpecial(XL_PASTE_FORMATS)
        excel.CutCopyMode = False
        board.Range("N4").Value = "Impact alert"
        board.Range("O4").Value = "Low Impact alert"
        board.Range(f"N5:N{last}").Formula = IMPACT
        board.Range(f"O5:O{last}").Formula = LOW_IMPACT
        board.Range(f"K5:K{last}").Formula = REVIEW

        readme = wb.Worksheets("README")
        bridge = str(readme.Range("B5").Value or "")
        if "Impact alert" not in bridge:
            readme.Range("B5").Value = bridge + README_NOTE

        excel.CalculateFull()
        after = cf_count(wb)
        wb.Save()
        print(f"rows through {last}; conditional formats before {before} after {after}")
    finally:
        wb.Close(SaveChanges=False)
        excel.Quit()
    print(f"Wrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
