toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Compare REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP tab.

Validation run for the thresholds. Reads the graded players from 000 (read only),
finds each in a scratch workbook built by `load_leaderboard.py` with no
`--min-elig` (transferred players often carry Elig 0), and writes one row per
match with the band gap in tier steps. Bands come from the workbook's own
formulas, not a reimplementation.

Matching is normalized name plus a compatible position group. Telemetry team
names do not match the recap's abbreviations, so the team is printed for an
eyeball check instead of filtered on. Namesakes come out as AMBIGUOUS rows; keep
the one whose team matches. With no exact name, it falls back to last name plus
first initial and marks every candidate LOOSE; confirm those by team too.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
      --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
      --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
      --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
      [--baseline "<Drive>/008. ....xlsx"]

--baseline checks that every PlayerId in that workbook gets identical flags in
the scratch build. Any mismatch means the scratch build is wrong, not the
thresholds.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from difflib import SequenceMatcher

import openpyxl

TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
RECAP_TO_GROUPS = {
    "QB": {"QB"}, "RB": {"RB"}, "WR": {"WR"}, "TE": {"TE"},
    "OL": {"OT", "OG", "C"}, "IDL": {"IDL", "EDGE"}, "EDGE": {"EDGE", "IDL", "OB-LB"},
    "ILB": {"OB-LB"}, "LB": {"OB-LB"}, "CB": {"CB", "SAF"}, "SAF": {"SAF", "CB"},
}
FLAG_KEYS = ["Projected band", "Elite share", "REVIEW?", "Speed alert", "Traits graded"]
OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    # 000 name cells can hold non-breaking spaces; treat any non-letter as a break.
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z']+", " ", str(name).upper()).replace("'", "").split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):

"""Compare REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP tab.

Validation run for the thresholds. Reads the graded players from 000 (read only),
finds each in a scratch workbook built by `load_leaderboard.py` with no
`--min-elig` (transferred players often carry Elig 0), and writes one row per
match with the band gap in tier steps. Bands come from the workbook's own
formulas, not a reimplementation.

Matching is normalized name plus a compatible position group. Telemetry team
names do not match the recap's abbreviations, so the team is printed for an
eyeball check instead of filtered on. Namesakes come out as AMBIGUOUS rows; keep
the one whose team matches. With no exact name, it falls back to last name plus
first initial and marks every candidate LOOSE; confirm those by team too.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
      --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
      --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
      --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
      [--baseline "<Drive>/008. ....xlsx"]

--baseline checks that every PlayerId in that workbook gets identical flags in
the scratch build. Any mismatch means the scratch build is wrong, not the
thresholds.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import re
from collections import Counter
from difflib import SequenceMatcher

import openpyxl

TIERS = ["AA", "AL", "QS", "FRP", "LIM", "NGE"]
RECAP_TO_GROUPS = {
    "QB": {"QB"}, "RB": {"RB"}, "WR": {"WR"}, "TE": {"TE"},
    "OL": {"OT", "OG", "C"}, "IDL": {"IDL", "EDGE"}, "EDGE": {"EDGE", "IDL", "OB-LB"},
    "ILB": {"OB-LB"}, "LB": {"OB-LB"}, "CB": {"CB", "SAF"}, "SAF": {"SAF", "CB"},
}
FLAG_KEYS = ["Projected band", "Elite share", "REVIEW?", "Speed alert", "Traits graded"]
OUT_FIELDS = ["Table", "Recap name", "Recap pos", "Recap team", "Prev conf", "Baylor RK", "Match",
              "Player", "Pos", "Pos raw", "Team", "Snaps", "Sample", "Elig Yrs", "Traits graded",
              "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "Gap", "REVIEW?",
              "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Impact alert", "Low Impact alert", "Player Impact", "Adv stats elite",
              "Adv stats poor", "Best trait", "Best trait pct", "Worst trait", "Worst trait pct",
              "PlayerId"]


def norm(name):
    # 000 name cells can hold non-breaking spaces; treat any non-letter as a break.
    words = re.sub(r"[^A-Z']+", " ", str(name).upper()).replace("'", "").split()
    return [w for w in words if w not in ("JR", "SR", "II", "III", "IV")]


def read_recap(master):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(master, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    rows = list(wb["POST-PORTAL RECAP"].iter_rows(values_only=True))
    wb.close()
    header_i = next(i for i, r in enumerate(rows) if r and "NAME" in r)
    header = [str(h).strip() if h else "" for h in rows[header_i]]
    starts = [i for i, h in enumerate(header) if h == "POS"]
    tables = ["Other school", "Baylor acquired"]
    players = []
    for t, start in enumerate(starts):
        end = starts[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(starts) else len(header)
        cols = {header[i]: i for i in range(start, end) if header[i]}
        for r in rows[header_i + 1:]:
            name = r[cols["NAME"]] if cols["NAME"] < len(r) else None
            if not name or str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip().upper().startswith("TOTAL"):
                continue
            players.append({
                "Table": tables[min(t, 1)], "Recap name": str(name).strip(),
                "Recap pos": str(r[cols["POS"]]).strip(), "Baylor RK": str(r[cols["RK"]]).strip(),
                "Recap team": str(r[cols["PREV TEAM"]]).strip(),
                "Prev conf": str(r[cols["PREV CONF"]]).strip(),
            })
    return players


def read_board(path):
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    inp = wb["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    in_hdr, board_hdr = list(next(inp)), list(next(board))
    pid_i, raw_i, team_i = (in_hdr.index(h) for h in ("PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Prev Team"))
    out = {}
    for irow, brow in zip(inp, board):
        if irow[pid_i]:
            rec = dict(zip(board_hdr, brow))
            rec.update({"PlayerId": irow[pid_i], "Pos raw": irow[raw_i], "Team": irow[team_i]})
            out[irow[pid_i]] = rec
    wb.close()
    return out


def gap(band, rk):
    if band in TIERS and rk in TIERS:
        return TIERS.index(rk) - TIERS.index(band)
    return None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--master", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--scratch", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--prev-conf", required=True, help="comma list, e.g. G6,FCS or SEC,B12,B10,ACC")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    scratch = read_board(args.scratch)
    if args.baseline:
        base = read_board(args.baseline)
        missing = [p for p in base if p not in scratch]
        diff = [p for p in base if p in scratch and any(base[p][k] != scratch[p][k] for k in FLAG_KEYS)]
        print(f"integrity: {len(base)} baseline rows, {len(missing)} missing, {len(diff)} mismatched")

    confs = {c.strip().upper() for c in args.prev_conf.split(",")}
    recap = [p for p in read_recap(args.master) if p["Prev conf"].upper() in confs]
    by_name = {}
    for rec in scratch.values():
        by_name.setdefault(tuple(norm(rec["Player"])), []).append(rec)

    out, status = [], Counter()
    for p in recap:
        groups = RECAP_TO_GROUPS.get(p["Recap pos"].upper(), set())
        name = norm(p["Recap name"])
        hits = [r for r in by_name.get(tuple(name), []) if r["Pos"] in groups]
        match = "NONE" if not hits else "OK" if len(hits) == 1 else "AMBIGUOUS"
        if not hits and name:
            # Telemetry spells some first names differently (Kam / Kamren, Yakiri / Yakari).
            # Last names within a typo (Osunsamni / Osunsanmi) also count.
            hits = [r for key, recs in by_name.items() if key and key[0][0] == name[0][0]
                    and SequenceMatcher(None, key[-1], name[-1]).ratio() >= 0.85
                    for r in recs if r["Pos"] in groups]
            match = "LOOSE" if hits else "NONE"
        status[match] += 1
        for rec in hits or [{}]:
            row = {**p, "Match": match, **{k: rec.get(k) for k in OUT_FIELDS if k in rec}}
            row["Gap"] = gap(rec.get("Projected band"), p["Baylor RK"])
            out.append(row)

    with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=OUT_FIELDS, extrasaction="ignore")
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(out)
    print(f"{len(recap)} recap players, matches {dict(status)}; wrote {args.out}")
    for r in out:
        print(r["Match"], r["Recap pos"], r["Baylor RK"], r["Recap name"], "|", r.get("Pos"), r.get("Team"),
              r.get("Snaps"), "|", r.get("Projected band"), "gap", r["Gap"], "REVIEW", r.get("REVIEW?"),
              "PI", r.get("Player Impact"))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Open work: the position-by-position screening matrix

This is deliverable 009. It was renumbered on 2026-09-15: Eric approved running
the 2025 baseline load (008) first, so the matrix is drafted from what that
validation run shows. It was started on 2026-09-05 and never finished. Source criteria were gathered, approval was asked for, and the
session ended before anything was written.

## What it needs to be

A one-page decision matrix defining, per position, the minimum evidence that
earns a further look, which weaknesses are acceptable, and what the exception
paths are. Concrete proposed rules, not blanks for staff to fill in.

Label everything in it as proposed staff-review decisions, not as existing
workbook rules. The workbook's current thresholds are implemented but unproven.

## What Eric specified

- "Let's proceed with the first priority in the position-by-position matrix."
- "Propose minimums and exceptions for review."
- "There is also a role-mapping issue within the first gap: WR versus SLOT, END
  versus JACK, and CB versus STAR can have different requirements."
- "The thresholds haven't demonstrated recruiting usefulness yet."
- "Test known prospects, including players the filter misses. Measure both
  worthwhile reviews generated and worthwhile players overlooked, by position."
- "minimum thresholds for guys that are worth taking a further look at"

Do not collapse those roles into generic position groups.

## Role factors already in the workbook

| Role | Factors used |
|---|---|
| END | Strength at POA, Tackling, Block Destruction / Pass Rush |
| JACK | Pass Rush / Block Destruction, Tackling, Ability to Play in Space |
| CB | Man-to-Man Coverage, Transition Speed / Competitive Edge, Ball Skills |
| STAR | Man-to-Man Coverage, Tackling, Ball Skills |
| WR and SLOT | Shared core evaluation factors, separate size matrices |

## Telemetry to Baylor role mapping

- WR maps to WR, SLOT
- EDGE maps to END, JACK
- CB maps to CB, STAR
- SAF maps to SAF, STAR
- OB-LB maps to ILB, JACK
- C is graded on the OG/C tab

## Metric quirks to keep in mind

Traits and advanced stats are 0 to 100 percentiles against the same position
(FBS, 2019 to present). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph, QB Risk Level is a
text label, Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the portal grid, QB
decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection", DB coverage surfaces as
"EPA/Target".

Source: Codex session 01a0718d, 2026-09-05. The quoted lines above are Eric's
own words from that session. Everything else is drawn from the workbook and the
Drive folder's AGENTS.md.

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 007 is the latest, so the next
  one is 008.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 008 are on Drive. **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS +
  Group of Six leaderboard baseline: 8,761 players with Elig 1+, 879 REVIEW
  flags, 778 of them with Sample OK. Built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from
  22 CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`. Next number is 009.
- 2026-09-15 meeting with a player personnel staff member: strong buy-in; he
  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run (done
  2026-09-16), screening matrix (009), then the weekly refresh once 2026 data
  fills in.
- **Validation run, both halves (2026-09-16):** 39 graded players from 000
  `POST-PORTAL RECAP` with a band (19 FCS / G6, 20 Power Four). Bands: 12
  exact, 28 within one tier, and the data runs low (mean gap -0.77 tiers,
  -1.25 on Power Four). REVIEW caught 10 of 13 QS-or-better offensive players
  and 5 of 15 defensive players; it flagged 4 of 11 FRP players. No thresholds
  changed. Detail: `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.
- This work is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (pushed), not
  yet merged to main. Detail: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`.

## Settings currently implemented

- Elite percentile 75, poor percentile 25
- Minimum snaps 150 (LOW SAMPLE warns below this, does not suppress)
- Speed alert: Play Speed or Deep Speed at 90th percentile or higher, fires
  independently of the elite-share gate
- Review trigger: elite-trait share at or above 0.375
- Minimum graded traits to project a band: 2, else THIN

## Next

1. **Decided 2026-09-16** (see "Decisions" in the validation doc): add a
   Player Impact alert that fires like the speed alert; add a low Player Impact
   alert (a note, not a suppression); Tackling stays counted for IDL (removing
   it fixes none of the misses); do the Power Four run before 009 (done).
2. **Eric picks the Player Impact alert cut point:** 90+ (catches 6 of 13
   misses, alerts 1 of 7 FRP non-REVIEW players, adds 385 on 008) or 80+ (9 of
   13, alerts 4 of 7). Low Player Impact note at 10 or lower on REVIEW rows
   (138 on 008). Tables in the validation doc, "Combined".
3. **Deliverable 009, the screening matrix**, drafted from the validation
   results. See `docs/open-work.md`.
4. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in (weeks 5 to 6). The staff member
   runs it himself, so it may belong in Power Query inside the workbook.
5. Reconstruct `build2.py` (workbook construction). `load_leaderboard.py`
   covers the data load for leaderboard exports.

## Open questions

- Are the 75th percentile and 0.375 share thresholds useful for recruiting?
  Validation (n = 39): good on offense, weak on defense, and low against Power
  Four grades (8 of 9 AL-graded P4 players project below AL). The 2-trait OL set
  can only produce LIM/NGE, QS or AA. No LIM or NGE graded players in the
  sample, so rejection is untested.
- Why do Baylor's own players disagree most (Keaton Thomas AL to LIM, DJ
  Coleman QS to FRP with Player Impact 96, Lagway AL to NGE)?
- Recap Jordan Church (N. Carolina St) matched a Louisville RG in Telemetry;
  confirm same player.
- Elusiveness (Telemetry WR trait) is missing from the CROSSWALK, glossary and
  formulas, though Baylor's WR / SLOT YAC Ability descriptor says "Elusive."
  Add it as a counted trait (changes WR elite share) or as a secondary?
- SETTINGS has no SLOT size row, so slot receivers are sized against WR.
- Size versus Player Impact for proven undersized players; band sort versus a
  rank, given the no-composite rule.
- Merge `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` into main?
- Drive `CLAUDE.md` file table is stale, and Drive `AGENTS.md` §6 wrongly says
  only PORTAL INPUT headers must match.

## Gotchas

- REVIEW BOARD reads PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position, not header. Load
  with `load_leaderboard.py`; write workbooks only through Excel COM (openpyxl
  save strips the conditional formatting).
- Telemetry `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files
  (30 of 30 transfers matched). Elig 1+ means still eligible after this season.
  `Team` is the season's school, not a current value.
- **Validation P4 files are subsets.** In `_exports/2025_baseline/
  validation_fbs_fcs/`, only the two QB files are full; the 16
  `*_recap-subset.csv` hold only recap players. Fine for grading those players
  (percentiles do not change with scope), useless for sizing alerts.
- **Downloads from automation (2026-09-16):** with the Chrome window hidden or
  minimized (`document.hidden` true), screenshots and timers stall and
  scripted downloads stop after the first one, even with "allow multiple
  downloads" on. Download CSV is an `<a download>` blob link inside a Radix
  menu (open it with a pointerdown on "More options"; the blob is built when
  the menu opens, so reopen after the table loads). Workaround used: `fetch()`
  the blob in the page and read it back, about 1 KB per JavaScript return. For
  full exports, keep the window visible and click by hand or with real clicks.
  Mantine selects (scope, season, group) respond to mousedown + click on
  `[role=option]`. Leaderboard `Top End
  Speed` looks like a percentile, not mph.
- Leaderboard position codes are alignments: OWR/SWR, H/F/Y, LT/RT, LG/C/RG,
  DT/NT, UP/DOWN, ILB/OLB, FS/SS, OCB/SCB, ST. Both scripts map them; ST shows
  Baylor tab "?".
- 4,047 of 8,761 rows in 008 are NO DATA: Advanced-Stats-only players carry
  Player Impact but no traits. FCS has no Ball Skills values. 66 players sit in
  two position groups and keep the first file's position.
- Telemetry in the browser: Chrome's "Ask where to save each file" dialog
  freezes automation (Eric turned it off 2026-09-15). Switching Player Traits /
  Advanced Stats tabs resets season, scope and group. Scope "Clear selection"
  does not remove Power Four; untick the option. Click coordinates use the
  screenshot frame, not page pixels. The Advanced Stats group list adds K and P
  at the bottom. Check the table has rows before Download CSV (one TE export
  came back empty).
- Portal scrape: calendar arrows move two months; "Apply Filters" may need a
  second click; reload if Next is disabled on page 1; the table is virtualized
  (~20 rows in the DOM).

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 1 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 1` keeps players still eligible after the current season. Telemetry's
  `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files (verified
  2026-09-15), so do not add a year for an older season.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

`POST-PORTAL RECAP` tab (read only). First used 2026-09-16; results in
`docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.

    --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
    --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
    --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
    [--baseline "<Drive>/008. <name>.xlsx"]
```

- Build `--scratch` with `load_leaderboard.py` and **no** `--min-elig`, into a

1	# CLAUDE.md — PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)
2	
3	Context and working rules for any Claude session in this folder. Read this first.
4	Companion file: `LOG.md` (chronological record of what was built and when).
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. What this project is
9	
10	A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
11	**Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles** with the internal **S.T.A.Q.S.**
12	grading scale, so incoming portal data can be filtered down to the players who
13	actually deserve a scout's time.
14	
15	One system, two inputs:
16	
17	- The scout's **STAQS grade stays the grade of record**.
18	- Telemetry percentiles become **threshold flags** that say who to review and
19	  which STAQS factors the data already supports.
20	
21	Nothing is averaged, weighted, or blended into a composite. That was an
22	explicit design decision (see §5).
23	
24	**Owner / audience:** Eric Rash. Audience for the deliverables is the
25	recruiting and personnel staff, not analysts.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 2. Standing rules (do not violate)
30	
31	1. **Read-only in Telemetry.** Never edit, save, or submit anything in
32	   app.telemetry.fm. Scraping the rendered UI for read purposes is fine.
33	2. **Always create new files. Never overwrite.** Files are numbered; the next
34	   revision is `003. ...`. The master `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` is never
35	   modified under any circumstances.
36	3. **Don't try to read Telemetry's auth token or import its internal service
37	   classes.** This is blocked by the permission classifier. Scrape the rendered
38	   table instead.
39	4. **STAQS is the grade of record.** Data output is labeled as a starting point
40	   for the scout, never as a grade.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 3. Files in this folder
45	
46	| File | Role |
47	|---|---|
48	| `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` | **Master, read-only.** GRD SCALE, OFFENSE/DEFENSE EVAL KEY, SZ-SPD matrices, NIL/XFER pay scales, per-position tabs (QB, RB, WR, SLOT, TE, OT, OG, NT, END, JACK, ILB, CB, SAF, STAR, SPD). The authority for tiers and size-speed standards. |
49	| `001. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING.xlsx` | Template workbook with 7 sample WRs, showing the format. Created 2026-09-02. |
50	| `001. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS FRAMEWORK.docx` | Written framework/explainer for the same system. |
51	| `002. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026 LOADED).xlsx` | Proof of concept with 3,000 live portal players loaded. Created 2026-09-03. |
52	| `CLAUDE.md` | This file. |
53	| `LOG.md` | Development log. |
54	
55	Build scripts (`build2.py`, `load.py`) lived in the session container only and
56	are **not** in this folder. The logic they encode is documented on the README
57	tab of the workbook and in `LOG.md`.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system
62	
63	Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8–72**.
64	
65	Five critical factors (all positions):
66	
67	- **S**ize
68	- **T**oughness
69	- **A**thletic Flexibility
70	- **Q**uickness
71	- **S**peed
72	
73	Plus **3 position-specific factors**. QB has its own set of 8 factors.
74	
75	**Tiers** (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry's Scout
76	Reports > Settings):
77	
78	| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color in Telemetry |
79	|---|---|---|---|
80	| AA | 60–72 | 7–8 | green |
81	| AL | 48–59 | 5–6 | yellow |
82	| QS | 40–47 | 3–4 | black |
83	| FRP | 30–39 | 1–2 | grey |
84	| LIM | 24–29 | 0–1 | pink |
85	| NGE | 8–23 (dropdown 0–23) | 0 | red |
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 5. The bridge (how Telemetry maps to STAQS)
90	
91	- Telemetry percentile **≥ 75** → counts as an **elite trait** (a 9).
92	- Telemetry percentile **< 25** → counts as a **deficiency** (a 1).
93	- **Elite share** = elite traits ÷ graded traits. Share is used instead of a raw
94	  count because positions carry different numbers of Telemetry traits (OL has 2,
95	  LB has 8).
96	- Share maps to a **projected band** using the GRD SCALE cut lines:
97	  7/8 = .875 → AA, 5/8 = .625 → AL, 3/8 = .375 → QS, 1/8 = .125 → FRP,
98	  0 → LIM/NGE (NGE only when deficiencies outnumber elite traits by 2+ with no
99	  elite share).
100	- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
101	- **REVIEW** flag fires at elite share ≥ .375 (the QS floor).
102	- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed ≥ 90 ("documented difference making
103	  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
104	- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — GRD SCALE's "must be
105	  special and offer a role" exception.
106	- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps (Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
107	  roughly 100 snaps).
108	
109	All of these live on the **SETTINGS** tab and are editable there. Change them
110	there, not in formulas.
111	
112	**What data can and cannot grade:** data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
113	factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
114	proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
115	CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
116	data-graded.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 6. Workbook structure (001 / 002)
121	
122	Tabs, in order:
123	
124	- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
125	- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, projected-band cut lines, simplified size
126	  standards by position. *Edit here.*
127	- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
128	- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
129	- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
130	- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes → Baylor eval tabs → trait counts.
131	- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet. Yellow fill + blue text = type here.
132	  Grouped as Player Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats.
133	  Percentiles 0–100; blank or `-` where a position carries no metric.
134	  Column order need not match Telemetry, but **headers must**. HT in inches
135	  (6'1" = 73).
136	- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT row.
137	  Columns include Traits graded, Elite traits, Deficiencies, Elite share,
138	  Projected band, REVIEW?, Speed alert, Size-Speed alert, Critical deficiency,
139	  data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst
140	  trait, plus roster metadata.
141	
142	**Cell legend:** yellow fill with blue text = user input. Black text = formula.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## 7. Telemetry platform notes
147	
148	Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
149	scouting platform.
150	
151	- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore tabs. Traits
152	  and stats only appear after filtering to a position or position group.
153	- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the internal Player Grade dropdown
154	  (already loaded with the six STAQS tiers). Scout reports carry a numeric Score
155	  (0–72) plus the grade.
156	- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
157	  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm — these PDFs are the reliable source
158	  for metric definitions.
159	- Traits and advanced stats are **0–100 percentiles vs the same position**
160	  (FBS, 2019–present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph;
161	  QB Risk Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking appears in the docs but not in
162	  the portal grid. QB decision-making shows as "Target Selection"; the DB
163	  coverage stat shows as "EPA/Target".
164	- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data — grade them on the STAQS
165	  eval keys as usual.
166	
167	### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)
168	
169	- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows rendered) with 100 rows per page.
170	  Scrape by scrolling the table's scroll container and clicking "Next page"
171	  (aria-label). Row key = name + Previous + Entered. ~3 s per page.
172	- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option),
173	  "Enter snap count" input, date range via calendar (each month arrow moves
174	  2 months; end date cannot exceed Telemetry's "today"). **Apply Filters
175	  sometimes needs a second click** — verify the "Filter (n)" count afterward.
176	- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload the page. The filter
177	  persists across reloads but window state does not, so **export scraped data
178	  first**.
179	- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64; oversized tool output is
180	  saved to a file in the container automatically.
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 8. Current state and next step
185	
186	Proof of concept (002) covers **3,000 portal players** who entered on or after
187	1/1/2026 with 100+ snaps and an FBS/FCS previous team:
188	WR 453, CB 431, IDL 311, EDGE 303, SAF 290, OB-LB 256, RB 231, OT 190, QB 156,
189	TE 156, OG 155, C 68.
190	
191	Results as of 2026-09-03: **608 REVIEW flags** (144 of them uncommitted),
192	**32 AA** and **133 AL** projections.
193	
194	**Next step Eric named:** once the approach is approved, automate the pull.

- Share maps to a **projected band** using the GRD SCALE cut lines:
  7/8 = .875 → AA, 5/8 = .625 → AL, 3/8 = .375 → QS, 1/8 = .125 → FRP,
  0 → LIM/NGE (NGE only when deficiencies outnumber elite traits by 2+ with no
  elite share).
- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** flag fires at elite share ≥ .375 (the QS floor).
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed ≥ 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps (Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps).

All of these live on the **SETTINGS** tab and are editable there. Change them
there, not in formulas.

**What data can and cannot grade:** data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (001 / 002)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, projected-band cut lines, simplified size
  standards by position. *Edit here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes → Baylor eval tabs → trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet. Yellow fill + blue text = type here.
  Grouped as Player Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats.
  Percentiles 0–100; blank or `-` where a position carries no metric.
  Column order need not match Telemetry, but **headers must**. HT in inches
  (6'1" = 73).
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT row.
  Columns include Traits graded, Elite traits, Deficiencies, Elite share,
  Projected band, REVIEW?, Speed alert, Size-Speed alert, Critical deficiency,
  data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst
  trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill with blue text = user input. Black text = formula.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore tabs. Traits
  and stats only appear after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the internal Player Grade dropdown
  (already loaded with the six STAQS tiers). Scout reports carry a numeric Score
  (0–72) plus the grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm — these PDFs are the reliable source
  for metric definitions.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0–100 percentiles vs the same position**
  (FBS, 2019–present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph;
  QB Risk Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking appears in the docs but not in
  the portal grid. QB decision-making shows as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat shows as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data — grade them on the STAQS
  eval keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows rendered) with 100 rows per page.
  Scrape by scrolling the table's scroll container and clicking "Next page"
  (aria-label). Row key = name + Previous + Entered. ~3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option),
  "Enter snap count" input, date range via calendar (each month arrow moves
  2 months; end date cannot exceed Telemetry's "today"). **Apply Filters
  sometimes needs a second click** — verify the "Filter (n)" count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload the page. The filter
  persists across reloads but window state does not, so **export scraped data
  first**.
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64; oversized tool output is
  saved to a file in the container automatically.

---

## 8. Current state and next step

Proof of concept (002) covers **3,000 portal players** who entered on or after
1/1/2026 with 100+ snaps and an FBS/FCS previous team:
WR 453, CB 431, IDL 311, EDGE 303, SAF 290, OB-LB 256, RB 231, OT 190, QB 156,
TE 156, OG 155, C 68.

Results as of 2026-09-03: **608 REVIEW flags** (144 of them uncommitted),
**32 AA** and **133 AL** projections.

**Next step Eric named:** once the approach is approved, automate the pull.

Eric asked this on 2026-09-16. It is by design, not a load error. 008 / 009
hold only players whose **2025 team was FCS or Group of Six** and who have
**Elig 1 or more** (Telemetry's current value: seasons left after 2026).

  2025 at a Power Four school, so they are outside the scope.

  after 2026. The 10 Baylor-acquired FCS / G6 players on the recap split
  exactly on that: in 009 are Logan Moore, Asher Hale, Cole Rhett, Kedrick
  Walker and Stilton McKelvey (Elig 1+); missing are Yakiri Walker, Jamaal
  Whyce, Kam Washington, Jordan Mack and Garrick Ponder (Elig 0).

  no row at all.

the Telemetry list "BU ROSTER 26" as scope and no eligibility filter. To
confirm the rule, check that exactly the FCS / G6 + Elig 1+ members of that
list are in 009.

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds, band cut lines, simplified size standards by
  position. *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the paste sheet, 67 columns in 002. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions) / QB Traits / Advanced Stats. Percentiles 0-100; blank
  or `-` where a position carries no metric. Column order need not match
  Telemetry but **headers must**. HT in inches (6'1" = 73).
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row (3,154 in 002). Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite
  share, projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, critical
  deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH / ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values,
  best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
  the reliable definition source.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
  keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
  count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.

---

## 8. Current state

Proof of concept (002 / 003 xlsx) covers **3,000 portal players** who entered on
or after 1/1/2026 with 100+ snaps and an FBS/FCS previous team:

WR 453 · CB 431 · IDL 311 · EDGE 303 · SAF 290 · OB-LB 256 · RB 231 · OT 190 ·
QB 156 · TE 156 · OG 155 · C 68

Results as of 2026-09-03: **608 REVIEW flags** (144 of them uncommitted),
**32 AA** and **133 AL** projections.

Known data caution: Top End Speed (the raw mph field) has implausible scraped
values, e.g. 39 mph. Verify against Telemetry before quoting it. It feeds no
flag today.

Teaching case used in the coach-facing docs: **Michael Gravely Jr.** (SAF, Ball
State) — 5 elite of 7 traits, so an AL projection, but Player Impact in the 1st
percentile. The traits-versus-production example.

---

## 9. Next steps for an agent picking this up

Eric's stated next step: **once the approach is approved, automate the pull.**
Concretely, in priority order:

1. **Reconstruct the build as versioned code in this folder.** `build2.py`
   (workbook construction) and `load.py` (data load) exist only in a dead
   session container. Rebuild them from §5-6 with openpyxl so the workbook is
   reproducible from a data file rather than by hand.
2. **Automate the scrape** per §7, with the gotchas encoded as retries and
   assertions (the second Apply Filters click, the Filter (n) verification, the
   page-1 reload, export-before-reload).
3. **Add a refresh path** that regenerates the REVIEW BOARD against a new pull
   without touching prior numbered files. New pull = new numbered workbook.
4. **Add validation**: flag implausible raw values (Top End Speed), report trait
   coverage by position, and diff a new pull against the prior one so staff see
   who is newly flagged.

Things deliberately out of scope: a weighted composite score, any write
operation against Telemetry, and data-grading of FBI, wiring, keep-ability,
character, or medical.

---

## 10. Conventions for whatever you write

- New deliverables are numbered; the next is `006.`. Never overwrite an existing
  numbered file, and never touch `000.`.
- Scripts go in this folder with plain names (`scrape_portal.py`,
  `build_workbook.py`), not numbered.
- Python with openpyxl for workbooks; the docs were built with docx-js.
- Deletion is not permitted from the agent session on this machine. Move
  unwanted files into `_to_delete/` and tell Eric.
- Append a dated entry to `LOG.md` for anything you build or decide.

flag today.

- **009** is the current workbook: 2025 FCS + Group of Six leaderboard players

mph. Verify before quoting it. It feeds no flag.

   without touching prior numbered files. New pull = new numbered workbook.

   coverage by position, and diff a new pull against the prior one so staff see
   who is newly flagged.

"""Validate a grading workbook (009 layout) against the documented algorithm.

Read only; never writes the workbook. Checks, each reported PASS or FAIL:

1. tabs          all eight tabs present, in order
2. settings      SETTINGS labels at the cells the formulas use (B5:B12, band
                 table A17:A20), values numeric
3. headers       PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD headers where the fixed-position
                 formulas expect them
4. formulas      key REVIEW BOARD formulas point at the right SETTINGS cells, and
                 every data row carries the same formula as row 5 (no hand edits)
5. errors        no #REF!, #VALUE! or other error values on REVIEW BOARD
6. cond-format   REVIEW BOARD conditional formatting present, alert highlight
                 covers L:O
7. recompute     every row's Traits graded, Elite traits, Deficiencies, Elite
                 share, Projected band, Sample, Speed alert, Impact alert,
                 REVIEW? and Low Impact alert recomputed in Python from PORTAL
                 INPUT + SETTINGS (AGENTS.md section 5) and compared with the
                 values Excel calculated

Exit code 0 only if every check passes. The workbook must have been saved by
Excel (cached values present), which every build script here does.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/check_workbook.py <workbook.xlsx> [--max-report 10]
"""

import argparse
import re
import sys
import zipfile
from collections import Counter

import openpyxl

TABS = ["README", "SETTINGS", "GRADE SCALE", "METRIC GLOSSARY", "CROSSWALK",
        "POSITION MAP", "PORTAL INPUT", "REVIEW BOARD"]
SETTINGS_LABELS = {
    "A5": "Elite percentile", "A6": "Poor percentile", "A7": "Minimum snaps",
    "A8": "Speed alert", "A9": "Review trigger", "A10": "Minimum graded traits",
    "A11": "Player Impact alert", "A12": "Low Impact alert",
    "A16": "Minimum elite share",
}
BANDS = {"A17": "AA", "A18": "AL", "A19": "QS", "A20": "FRP"}
INPUT_HEADERS = {"A": "Player", "B": "Pos (Telemetry)", "H": "Snaps", "P": "Play Speed",
                 "Q": "Deep Speed", "AC": "Tackling", "AD": "Accuracy",
                 "AI": "Target Selection", "AJ": "Player Impact", "BN": "Penalty Drawn",
                 "BO": "Notes", "BP": "PlayerId"}
BOARD_HEADERS = ["Player", "Pos", "Baylor tab", "Snaps", "Sample", "Traits graded",
                 "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band", "REVIEW?",
                 "Speed alert", "Size-Speed alert", "Impact alert", "Low Impact alert"]
KEY_FORMULA_PARTS = {
    "E": ["SETTINGS!$B$7"],
    "J": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$A$17", "SETTINGS!$A$18", "SETTINGS!$A$19", "SETTINGS!$A$20"],
    "K": ["SETTINGS!$B$10", "SETTINGS!$B$9", 'L5="Y"', 'N5="Y"', "F5=0"],
    "L": ["SETTINGS!$B$8", "'PORTAL INPUT'!P5", "'PORTAL INPUT'!Q5"],
    "N": ["SETTINGS!$B$11", "'PORTAL INPUT'!AJ5"],
    "O": ["SETTINGS!$B$12", 'K5="Y"'],
}
RECOMPUTED = ["Traits graded", "Elite traits", "Deficiencies", "Elite share", "Projected band",
              "Sample", "Speed alert", "Impact alert", "REVIEW?", "Low Impact alert"]
REF = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z_$])(\$?)([A-Z]{1,3})(\$?)(\d+)(?![\d(])")


def col(letter):
    n = 0
    for ch in letter:
        n = n * 26 + ord(ch) - 64
    return n - 1


def shift(formula, rows):
    """Row 5 formula -> the same formula written for a later row."""
    def repl(m):
        if m.group(3):
            return m.group(0)
        return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}{m.group(3)}{int(m.group(4)) + rows}"
    return REF.sub(repl, formula)


def num(v):
    return v if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) else None


def blank(v):
    return v is None or v == ""


class Report:
    def __init__(self, max_report):
        self.results, self.max = [], max_report

    def add(self, name, problems, detail=""):
        ok = not problems
        self.results.append(ok)
        print(f"[{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {name}{': ' + detail if detail else ''}")
        for p in problems[:self.max]:
            print(f"        {p}")
        if len(problems) > self.max:
            print(f"        ... {len(problems) - self.max} more")


def cond_format(path):
    """Count conditionalFormatting blocks on REVIEW BOARD straight from the xlsx XML."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        wb_xml = z.read("xl/workbook.xml").decode("utf8")
        rels = z.read("xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels").decode("utf8")

    ap.add_argument("--max-report", type=int, default=10)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    rep = Report(args.max_report)

    wf = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True)
    wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(args.workbook, read_only=True, data_only=True)

    rep.add("tabs", [] if wf.sheetnames == TABS else [f"found {wf.sheetnames}"])

    sv = {c.coordinate: c.value for row in wv["SETTINGS"].iter_rows(min_row=1, max_row=21, max_col=3)
          for c in row if hasattr(c, "coordinate")}
    probs = [f"{cell} is {sv.get(cell)!r}, expected to start {label!r}"
             for cell, label in SETTINGS_LABELS.items() if not str(sv.get(cell) or "").startswith(label)]
    probs += [f"B{r} is {sv.get(f'B{r}')!r}, not a number" for r in range(5, 13) if num(sv.get(f"B{r}")) is None]
    probs += [f"{cell} band is {sv.get('B' + cell[1:])!r}, expected {band}"
              for cell, band in BANDS.items() if sv.get("B" + cell[1:]) != band or num(sv.get(cell)) is None]
    rep.add("settings", probs)
    S = {k: sv.get(k) for k in ("B5", "B6", "B7", "B8", "B9", "B10", "B11", "B12", "A17", "A18", "A19", "A20")}

    inp_rows = wv["PORTAL INPUT"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    inp_head = list(next(inp_rows))
    probs = [f"PORTAL INPUT {c}4 is {inp_head[col(c)]!r}, expected {h!r}"
             for c, h in INPUT_HEADERS.items() if col(c) >= len(inp_head) or inp_head[col(c)] != h]
    board_vals = wv["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
    board_head = list(next(board_vals))
    probs += [f"REVIEW BOARD column {i + 1} is {board_head[i]!r}, expected {h!r}"
              for i, h in enumerate(BOARD_HEADERS) if i >= len(board_head) or board_head[i] != h]
    rep.add("headers", probs)
    if probs:
        print("Stopping: layout is not the 009 layout, so later checks would be meaningless.")
        return 1

    board_f = wf["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=5)
    first = next(board_f)
    base = {c.column_letter: c.value for c in first if isinstance(c.value, str) and c.value.startswith("=")}
    probs = [f"{letter}5 formula missing {part!r}" for letter, parts in KEY_FORMULA_PARTS.items()
             for part in parts if part not in (base.get(letter) or "")]
    drift, rows_checked = [], 1
    for row in board_f:
        cells = [c for c in row if hasattr(c, "column_letter")]
        if not cells:
            continue
        r = cells[0].row
        rows_checked += 1
        for c in cells:
            if c.column_letter in base:
                want = shift(base[c.column_letter], r - 5)
                if c.value != want:
                    drift.append(f"{c.column_letter}{r} = {str(c.value)[:70]!r} (expected the row-5 formula)")
    rep.add("formulas", probs + drift, f"{len(base)} formula columns x {rows_checked} rows")

    board = [dict(zip(board_head, r)) for r in board_vals]
    inputs = [r for r in inp_rows]
    errs = [f"row {i + 5} {k} = {v}" for i, row in enumerate(board) for k, v in row.items()
            if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("#")]
    rep.add("errors", errs)

    sq = cond_format(args.workbook)
    probs = [] if sq else ["no conditional formatting on REVIEW BOARD (saved with openpyxl?)"]
    if sq and not any(s.startswith("L5:O") for s in sq):
        probs.append(f"alert highlight does not cover L:O; ranges {sq}")
    rep.add("cond-format", probs, f"{len(sq)} rules")

    P, Q, H, AJ = col("P"), col("Q"), col("H"), col("AJ")
    traits = range(col("P"), col("AI") + 1)
    mism, counts = Counter(), Counter()
    examples = []
    for i, (row, got) in enumerate(zip(inputs, board)):
        if blank(row[0]):
            continue
        vals = [num(row[j]) for j in traits]
        graded = [v for v in vals if v is not None]
        F = len(graded)
        G = sum(v >= S["B5"] for v in graded)
        D = sum(v < S["B6"] for v in graded)
        share = G / F if F else None
        if F == 0:
            band = "NO DATA"
        elif F < S["B10"]:
            band = "THIN"
        elif share >= S["A17"]:
            band = "AA"
        elif share >= S["A18"]:
            band = "AL"
        elif share >= S["A19"]:
            band = "QS"
        elif share >= S["A20"]:
            band = "FRP"
        else:
            band = "NGE" if D >= G + 2 else "LIM"
        sample = "LOW SAMPLE" if (num(row[H]) or 0) < S["B7"] else "OK"
        speed = "Y" if max(num(row[P]) or 0, num(row[Q]) or 0) >= S["B8"] else None
        impact = "Y" if not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) >= S["B11"] else None
        review = "Y" if F > 0 and ((F >= S["B10"] and share >= S["B9"]) or speed or impact) else None
        low = "Y" if review and not blank(row[AJ]) and (num(row[AJ]) or 0) <= S["B12"] else None
        want = {"Traits graded": F, "Elite traits": G, "Deficiencies": D, "Elite share": share,
                "Projected band": band, "Sample": sample, "Speed alert": speed,
                "Impact alert": impact, "REVIEW?": review, "Low Impact alert": low}
        counts["rows"] += 1
        counts["REVIEW"] += review == "Y"
        for k in RECOMPUTED:
            a, b = want[k], got.get(k)
            a = None if a in ("",) else a
            b = None if b in ("",) else b
            same = (abs(a - b) < 1e-9) if isinstance(a, float) and isinstance(b, (int, float)) else a == b
            if not same:
                mism[k] += 1
                if len(examples) < args.max_report:
                    examples.append(f"row {i + 5} {row[0]}: {k} workbook {b!r}, recomputed {a!r}")
    detail = f"{counts['rows']} rows, {counts['REVIEW']} REVIEW recomputed"
    rep.add("recompute", [f"{k}: {n} rows differ" for k, n in mism.items()] + examples, detail)

    ok = all(rep.results)
    print("RESULT:", "ALL CHECKS PASS" if ok else "FAILED")
    return 0 if ok else 1

# scripts

## load_leaderboard.py

Loads Telemetry **leaderboard** CSV exports (Leaderboards > Player Traits or
Advanced Stats > "..." > Download CSV) into a new numbered grading workbook. It
is the data-load half of the lost `load.py`, rebuilt for leaderboard exports.

```
uv run --with openpyxl --with pywin32 python scripts/load_leaderboard.py ^
    --csv-dir "<folder of downloaded CSVs>" ^
    --template "<Drive>\003. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (PORTAL 2026, BAYLOR STYLE).xlsx" ^
    --stage-dir "<scratch folder>" ^
    --min-elig 1 ^
    --out "<Drive>\008. <name>.xlsx"
```

Omit `--out` to stage only (no Excel): writes `portal_input_stage.csv` and
`load_report.json` to `--stage-dir`.

What it does:

- Reads PORTAL INPUT row 4 headers from the template, so the column order always
  matches the formulas (they read by fixed position, not header).
- Joins Player Traits and Advanced Stats rows on the CSV's `PlayerId`.
- Maps header names that differ (`Pos.`, `Elig.`, `Weight`, `Team`, throw
  velocities, Top End Speed). Converts Height `6-2` to inches. Folds State into
  Hometown. Team slug goes into Prev Team.
- Maps leaderboard position codes to POSITION MAP codes (OWR and SWR to WR, and
  the POSITION MAP aliases). The raw code is kept.
- `--min-elig 1` keeps players still eligible after the current season. Telemetry's
  `Elig.` and `Class` are current values even in past-season files (verified
  2026-09-15), so do not add a year for an older season.
- PlayerId, raw position, Elusiveness and source file go in columns after Notes.
  Columns A:BO keep their meaning, so REVIEW BOARD, traits graded and elite share
  are unchanged.
- Builds the workbook through **Excel COM**, never openpyxl save (that strips the
  conditional formatting). Refuses to overwrite an existing file. Extends
  PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD rows past the template's last row when needed.

Check `load_report.json` after every run: `unmapped_csv_headers` and
`unknown_position_codes` must be empty or explained before using the workbook.

Data stays on Drive or in a scratch folder. Never commit CSVs, stage files or
workbooks here.

## file_exports.py

Files Telemetry leaderboard downloads from the Downloads folder into a Drive
export folder with consistent names, identifying each file by content (Chrome
often leaves them as `<uuid>.tmp`).

```
uv run python scripts/file_exports.py --downloads "C:/Users/eric_rash/Downloads" ^
    --dest "<Drive>/PP_Recruiting/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
    --prefix 2025_fcs-g6 --since "2026-09-15 16:00" [--dry-run]
```

- Tab from the header (`Player Impact` present = Advanced Stats), group from the
  `Pos.` codes (OWR/SWR to WR, OG/C to IOL).
- Names files `<prefix>_<GROUP>_<player-traits|advanced-stats>.csv`.
- Copies, verifies byte for byte, then deletes the download. Never overwrites;
  duplicates and unclear files are reported and left in Downloads.
- Run with `--dry-run` first.

## validate_recap.py

Validation run: compares REVIEW BOARD bands with Baylor grades on 000's
`POST-PORTAL RECAP` tab (read only). First used 2026-09-16; results in
`docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.

```
uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/validate_recap.py ^
    --master "<Drive>/000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx" ^
    --scratch "<scratch>/scratch_nofilter.xlsx" ^
    --prev-conf G6,FCS --out "<scratch>/validation.csv" ^
    [--baseline "<Drive>/008. <name>.xlsx"]
```

- Build `--scratch` with `load_leaderboard.py` and **no** `--min-elig`, into a
  scratch folder off Drive. Transferred players often carry Elig 0.
- `--prev-conf` picks recap rows by previous conference (`SEC,B12,B10,ACC` for
  the Power Four half).
- Match column: OK, AMBIGUOUS (namesakes), LOOSE (last name plus first initial,
  for spellings like Kam / Kamren), NONE. Confirm AMBIGUOUS and LOOSE rows by
  team before using them.
- `--baseline` checks the scratch build gives identical flags for every PlayerId
  in a numbered workbook.
- LOOSE also accepts a last name within a typo (difflib ratio 0.85, same first
  initial), for recap spellings like Osunsamni / Osunsanmi.
- The Power Four input folder (`validation_fbs_fcs/`) is mostly
  `*_recap-subset.csv` files holding only recap players, so a scratch build from
  it has about 881 rows, not a full population. Do not size alerts from it.

## add_impact_alerts.py

Adds the Impact alert and Low Impact alert (decided 2026-09-16) to a grading
workbook built on the 003 layout. Built 009 from 008.

```
uv run --with pywin32 python scripts/add_impact_alerts.py ^
    --in "<Drive>/008. <name>.xlsx" --out "<scratch>/009 build.xlsx"
```

- Copies `--in` to a new `--out` (refuses to overwrite) and edits the copy
  through Excel COM, so references shift and formatting survives.
- SETTINGS rows 11-12: Impact alert cut point (90), Low Impact cut point (10).
  The band table moves down two rows; formulas follow automatically.
- REVIEW BOARD N "Impact alert", O "Low Impact alert", after Size-Speed alert.
  REVIEW? (K) now ORs in the Impact alert, like the speed alert. No-trait rows
  still never show REVIEW.
- Stops if the layout is not the expected one or the alerts already exist.
- 009 already has the alerts, so use **009 as the `load_leaderboard.py`
  template** from now on; do not run this script on it again.

Verify after a build: zero formula errors, bands identical to the source, every
source REVIEW row still REVIEW.

`load_leaderboard.py` needs an existing workbook (003) as its template rather
than building one from scratch.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

- Deliverables 001 to 009 are on Drive. Next number is 010.
- **009** (2026-09-16) is 008 plus the Impact alert (Player Impact 90+, turns
  REVIEW on) and the Low Impact alert (REVIEW rows at Player Impact 10 or
  lower, a note only). 1,264 REVIEW flags (was 879), 1,163 with Sample OK (was
  778); all 385 new flags come from the Impact alert. 149 Low Impact alerts.
  Bands unchanged. Built by `scripts/add_impact_alerts.py` from 008; use 009 as
  the template for future loads.
- **008** (2026-09-15) is the 2025 FCS + Group of Six leaderboard baseline:
  8,761 players with Elig 1+, built by `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` from 22
  CSVs in Drive `_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6/`.
- 2026-09-15 meeting with a player personnel staff member: strong buy-in; he
  wants 30 to 50 pre-portal names per position by week 5 or 6. Notes:
  `docs/2026-09-15-review-board-meeting.md`.
- Plan approved by Eric 2026-09-15: 2025 baseline (done), validation run (done
  2026-09-16), alerts (009, done), screening matrix (010), then the weekly
  refresh once 2026 data fills in.
- **Validation run, both halves (2026-09-16):** 39 graded players from 000
  `POST-PORTAL RECAP` with a band (19 FCS / G6, 20 Power Four). Bands: 12
  exact, 28 within one tier, and the data runs low (mean gap -0.77 tiers,
  -1.25 on Power Four). REVIEW caught 10 of 13 QS-or-better offensive players
  and 5 of 15 defensive players; it flagged 4 of 11 FRP players. With 009's
  Impact alert: 21 of 28 QS-or-better caught, 5 of 11 FRP flagged. Detail:
  `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`.
- This work is on branch `worktree-fireflies-review-board-0915` (pushed), not

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

All workarounds were tried and ruled out (see STATUS gotchas and the last LOG
entry). Do not retry them.

## Next steps once Eric says "go"

1. **Full 2025 FBS leaderboard pull.** Leaderboards > Player Traits and Advanced
   Stats, season 2025, scope FBS (untick Power Four), all 11 groups = 22 CSVs.
   Real clicks on the "More options" menu > Download CSV worked when visible.

   That makes the matrix deliverable 011: update `open-work.md`, STATUS, Drive

   evidence, acceptable weaknesses, exception paths; keep WR/SLOT, END/JACK,

   week 3). Deliverables use the Baylor design system (see Drive AGENTS.md §6).
4. Optional validation: scope Telemetry list "BU ROSTER 26", confirm exactly its
   FCS/G6 + Elig 1+ members appear in 009.
5. Weekly refresh design once 2026 data fills in (Power Query vs Python).

- Telemetry is read-only; never read its auth token or import internal classes.
- Never overwrite numbered files; never touch `000.`. Write workbooks only via
  Excel COM (openpyxl saves drop cached values and CF extensions).
- REVIEW BOARD reads PORTAL INPUT by fixed column position.
- Session is a worktree: use plain, simple shell commands (complex/compound
  commands get refused); commit and push before ending; merges to main only
  when Eric asks (use a PR, as with PR #1).
- Writing style: plain, direct, no em dashes. Append a dated LOG.md entry for any
  numbered file, decision, or proven/ruled-out technique.

## Suggested skills

- `claude-in-chrome` before any browser work (the FBS pull).
- `superpowers:verification-before-completion` before claiming the pull, the
  workbook, or the matrix is done (run `check_workbook.py`, spot-check snaps).
- `anthropic-skills:docx` (or `artifact-design` if Eric wants a page) for the
  screening matrix document.
- `memory-write` to update the PP Recruiting line in global working memory at
  the end.
- `closeout` at session end if Eric asks to wrap up.
